    // 3e (W.8): the strikes the account was given, after its reports.
    strikes: [],
    // Then its standing measures, its replies and its report counts.
    standing: [
      {
        decisionId: h.removalId,
        kind: "suspend",
        basis: "threat",
        days: 7,
        announced: false,
        decidedAt: iso(T0 - 3 * DAY_MS),
        earliestStart: iso(T0 - 3 * DAY_MS),
        startsAt: iso(T0 - 3 * DAY_MS),
        endsAt: iso(T0 - DAY_MS),
        liftedAt: iso(T0 - DAY_MS),
        liftedBy: h.correctionId,
        replaced: false,
        basisEndedAt: null,
        basisEndedBy: null,
      },
    ],
    replies: [{ decisionId: h.removalId, filedAt: iso(T0 - 2 * DAY_MS), onTime: false, text: "I did not write that post.", erasedAt: null, answeredAt: iso(T0 - DAY_MS), answeredBy: h.correctionId }],
    reporting: {
      frameDays: 90,
      days: [{ day: "2026-09-11", reports: 2 }],
      marks: [{ ref: "N-ABCDEFGH24", position: 1, sentOn: "2026-09-11", markedAt: iso(T0 - DAY_MS), withdrawnAt: null, counts: true }],
      markedReports: 1,
    },
    // 3d (W.10): the refused upload and the release, last, each in the format's order.
    uploads: [
      {
        id: h.removalId,
        refusedAt: iso(T0 - 3 * DAY_MS),
        source: "test",
        matchKind: "exact",
        listedAs: "csam",
        objection: { text: "It is my own photo.", objectedAt: iso(T0 - 2 * DAY_MS) },
        mayObject: false,
        endedAt: iso(T0 - 2 * DAY_MS),
        endAs: "report",
        endReason: null,
        released: iso(T0 - DAY_MS),
        reportKept: true,
      },
    ],
    releases: [{ id: h.correctionId, basis: "leave", releasedAt: iso(T0 - DAY_MS), upload: true }],
  };
}

/** More rows in every list than a few pages of two hold: text that JSON escapes, a line break inside a body, characters outside ASCII. */
function addManyRows(h: Harness): void {
  const quote = String.fromCharCode(34);
  const newline = String.fromCharCode(10);
  const accented = `caf${String.fromCharCode(0xe9)} ${String.fromCodePoint(0x1f600)}`;
  for (let i = 0; i < 5; i++) {
    h.lists.posts.push({
      id: randomUUID(),
      body: `post ${i}: ${quote}quoted${quote}${newline}second line, ${accented}`,
      createdAt: new Date(T0 - DAY_MS + i),
      replyToId: i % 2 === 0 ? h.postId : null,
      quoteOfId: i === 3 ? h.postId : null,
      state: i === 4 ? "withheld" : "visible",
      deletedAt: null,
      media: i === 1 ? [{ id: randomUUID(), altText: `alt ${accented}`, width: 10, height: 20 }] : [],
    });
  }
  for (let i = 0; i < 6; i++) h.lists.likes.push({ postId: randomUUID(), at: new Date(T0 - 900 + i) });
  for (let i = 0; i < 3; i++) h.lists.reposts.push({ postId: randomUUID(), at: new Date(T0 - 800 + i) });
  for (let i = 0; i < 4; i++) h.lists.bookmarks.push({ postId: randomUUID(), at: new Date(T0 - 700 + i) });
  for (let i = 0; i < 5; i++) h.lists.following.push({ handle: `friend_${i}`, since: new Date(T0 - 600 + i) });
  for (let i = 0; i < 2; i++) h.lists.blocks.push({ handle: `blocked_${i}`, since: new Date(T0 - 500 + i) });
  for (let i = 0; i < 3; i++) h.lists.mutes.push({ handle: `muted_${i}`, since: new Date(T0 - 400 + i) });
}

/** How many reads a list of `rows` takes in pages of `size`: full pages, then the short (maybe empty) one that says it is over. */
const readsFor = (rows: number, size: number) => Math.floor(rows / size) + 1;

describe("building the export", () => {
  test("the JSON follows the contract, marks the current session, lists the passkeys with nothing of their keys, and keeps a deleted post with its empty body and deletion time", async () => {
    const h = harness();
    const plan = await buildExport(h.deps, h.userId, h.currentSession, h.now());
    const json = ExportFormat.parse(JSON.parse((await collect(exportJson(plan))).join("")));
    expect(json.format).toBe("korbat-export-1");
    expect(json.exportedAt).toBe(iso(T0));
    expect(json.account).toEqual({
      id: h.userId,
      email: "ada@korbat.local",
      createdAt: iso(T0 - 3 * DAY_MS),
      role: "user",
      mfaEnabled: true,
      hasPassword: false,
      verified: true,
      termsVersion: "draft-test",
      termsAcceptedAt: iso(T0 - 3 * DAY_MS),
      // Inside the account, in the auth module's order (newest first), each as the five facts with the times as ISO text.
      passkeys: [
        { name: "Security key", createdAt: iso(T0 - DAY_MS), lastUsedAt: null, synced: false, createdOn: null },
        { name: "Laptop", createdAt: iso(T0 - 2 * DAY_MS), lastUsedAt: iso(T0 - DAY_MS), synced: true, createdOn: "Chrome on Windows" },
      ],
    });
    expect(json.sessions).toEqual([
      { id: h.otherSession, createdAt: iso(T0 - 2 * DAY_MS), lastUsedAt: iso(T0 - DAY_MS), current: false },
      { id: h.currentSession, createdAt: iso(T0 - DAY_MS), lastUsedAt: iso(T0), current: true },
    ]);
    expect(json.devices).toEqual([{ label: "Chrome on Windows", platform: "web", firstSeenAt: iso(T0 - 3 * DAY_MS), lastSeenAt: iso(T0) }]);
    expect(json.events).toEqual([
      { type: "signin_success", at: iso(T0 - DAY_MS) },
      { type: "signup", at: iso(T0 - 3 * DAY_MS) },
    ]);
    // With the author's Explore switch as the profile holds it (off here); the byte-for-byte tests below place it after the handle history.
    expect(json.profile).toEqual({ handle: "ada", displayName: "Ada", bio: "Analytical engines.", createdAt: iso(T0 - 3 * DAY_MS), handleHistory: ["ada_old", "ada"], showInExplore: false, retiredHandles: [{ handle: "ada_old", retiredAt: iso(T0 - DAY_MS) }] });
    expect(json.posts).toHaveLength(2);
    expect(json.posts[0]).toEqual({
      id: h.postId,
      body: "two photos",
      createdAt: iso(T0 - 2 * DAY_MS),
      replyToId: null,
      quoteOfId: null,
      state: "visible",
      deletedAt: null,
      media: [
        { id: h.imageA, file: `media/${h.imageA}.webp`, altText: "a harbour at dawn", width: 1600, height: 1200 },
        { id: h.imageB, file: `media/${h.imageB}.webp`, altText: "a lighthouse", width: 900, height: 1600 },
      ],
    });
    expect(json.posts[1]).toEqual({ id: h.deletedId, body: "", createdAt: iso(T0 - DAY_MS), replyToId: h.postId, quoteOfId: null, state: "deleted_by_author", deletedAt: iso(T0 - 1_000), media: [] });
    expect(json.likes).toEqual([{ postId: h.likedId, at: iso(T0 - DAY_MS) }]);
    expect(json.reposts).toEqual([]);
    expect(json.bookmarks).toEqual([{ postId: h.bookmarkedId, at: iso(T0 - 500) }]);
    expect(json.following).toEqual([{ handle: "bob", since: iso(T0 - 2 * DAY_MS) }]);
    expect(json.blocks).toEqual([{ handle: "eve", since: iso(T0 - DAY_MS) }]);
    expect(json.mutes).toEqual([{ handle: "carol", since: iso(T0 - 200) }]);
    expect(json.missingMedia).toEqual([]);
    expect(plan.images).toEqual([]);
    // Building the plan records nothing: the event belongs after the last chunk of the stream.
    expect(h.events).toEqual([]);
  });

  test("the images to write are the media module's, and the entry name is media/<id>.webp", async () => {
    const h = harness();
    h.images.push({ id: randomUUID(), open: openerOf(path.join(root, "a")) }, { id: randomUUID(), open: openerOf(path.join(root, "b")) });
    const plan = await buildExport(h.deps, h.userId, h.currentSession, h.now());
    expect(plan.images).toEqual(h.images);
    expect(mediaEntry(h.images[0]!.id)).toBe(`media/${h.images[0]!.id}.webp`);
  });

  test("export.json is read list by list in pages and written piece by piece, byte for byte as JSON.stringify(document, null, 2) writes it", async () => {
    const h = harness();
    addManyRows(h);
    const plan = await buildExport(h.deps, h.userId, h.currentSession, h.now(), 2);
    // Only the account and the profile's own fields are read up front; the lists wait for the JSON to be written.
    expect(h.reads).toEqual([]);
    const text = (await collect(exportJson(plan))).join("");
    expect(text).toBe(JSON.stringify(expectedDocument(h), null, 2));
    expect(() => ExportFormat.parse(JSON.parse(text))).not.toThrow();
    // Every list was read in pages of two, one page after the other, in the document's order.
    const order: (keyof Lists)[] = ["posts", "likes", "reposts", "bookmarks", "following", "blocks", "mutes"];
    expect(h.reads).toEqual(order.flatMap((name) => Array.from({ length: readsFor(h.lists[name].length, 2) }, () => name)));
    // The same account in one page per list is the same text.
    const whole = await buildExport(h.deps, h.userId, h.currentSession, h.now());
    expect((await collect(exportJson(whole))).join("")).toBe(text);
  });

  test("empty lists and missing images are written as JSON.stringify writes them", async () => {
    const h = harness();
    for (const name of ["posts", "likes", "bookmarks", "following", "blocks", "mutes"] as const) h.lists[name].length = 0;
    const plan = await buildExport(h.deps, h.userId, h.currentSession, h.now(), 3);
    plan.missingMedia.push(h.imageA, h.imageB);
    expect((await collect(exportJson(plan))).join("")).toBe(JSON.stringify(expectedDocument(h, [h.imageA, h.imageB]), null, 2));
  });

  test("the moderation member is the document's last: read once, before the first byte, for the account that asks, and written with the format's members in the format's order and nothing else", async () => {
    const h = harness();
    const plan = await buildExport(h.deps, h.userId, h.currentSession, h.now());
    // Read with the account's own facts, before anything is written.
    expect(h.asked).toEqual([h.userId]);
    const text = (await collect(exportJson(plan))).join("");
    const raw = JSON.parse(text) as Record<string, unknown>;
    expect(Object.keys(raw).at(-1)).toBe("moderation");
    expect(raw.moderation).toStrictEqual(expectedModeration(h));
    // The contract reads it whole: nothing of it lies outside the format.
    expect(ExportFormat.parse(raw).moderation).toStrictEqual(raw.moderation);
    // Member for member in the format's order, though the module handed every object over in another one.
    const NL = String.fromCharCode(10);
    expect(text.endsWith(`,${NL}  "moderation": ${JSON.stringify(expectedModeration(h), null, 2).replaceAll(NL, `${NL}  `)}${NL}}`)).toBe(true);
    // What the module's objects carry beyond the format is not written.
    expect(text).not.toContain("decidedBy");
    expect(text).not.toContain("a staff member the export must never name");
    expect(h.asked).toEqual([h.userId]);
  });

  test("an account module built without the moderation module still writes the member, with empty lists and counts over the standing rules' frame", async () => {
    const h = harness();
    const deps: AccountDeps = { ...h.deps, moderation: undefined };
    const text = (await collect(exportJson(await buildExport(deps, h.userId, h.currentSession, h.now())))).join("");
    expect(text).toBe(JSON.stringify({ ...expectedDocument(h), moderation: { decisions: [], reports: [], strikes: [], standing: [], replies: [], reporting: { frameDays: STANDING_RULES.reportFrameDays, days: [], marks: [], markedReports: 0 }, uploads: [], releases: [] } }, null, 2));
    expect(() => ExportFormat.parse(JSON.parse(text))).not.toThrow();
    expect(h.asked).toEqual([]);
  });

  test("a large account's export.json comes in several pieces of at most 64 KiB of UTF-8", async () => {
    const h = harness();
    const accented = String.fromCharCode(0xe9).repeat(200);
    for (let i = 0; i < 3_000; i++) h.lists.likes.push({ postId: randomUUID(), at: new Date(T0 - 100_000 + i) });
    for (let i = 0; i < 1_000; i++) h.lists.posts.push({ id: randomUUID(), body: accented, createdAt: new Date(T0 - 50_000 + i), replyToId: null, quoteOfId: null, state: "visible", deletedAt: null, media: [] });
    const pieces = await collect(exportJson(await buildExport(h.deps, h.userId, h.currentSession, h.now())));
    expect(pieces.length).toBeGreaterThan(5);
    for (const piece of pieces) expect(Buffer.byteLength(piece, "utf8")).toBeLessThanOrEqual(KIB64);
    expect(pieces.join("")).toBe(JSON.stringify(expectedDocument(h), null, 2));
  });

  test("the file name carries the handle and the day of the export", () => {
    expect(exportFilename("ada_l", new Date("2026-09-24T23:59:59.000Z"))).toBe("korbat-export-ada_l-2026-09-24.zip");
  });

  test("one export a day: the second is rate_limited with a Retry-After, the next day is allowed again, and a store that fails closes the door", async () => {
    const h = harness();
    await enforceExportLimit(h.deps, h.userId);
    const refused = await enforceExportLimit(h.deps, h.userId).catch((err: unknown) => err);
    expect(refused).toBeInstanceOf(AccountError);
    expect((refused as AccountError).code).toBe("rate_limited");
    expect((refused as AccountError).status).toBe(429);
    expect((refused as AccountError).retryAfterSeconds).toBeGreaterThan(0);
    expect((refused as AccountError).retryAfterSeconds).toBeLessThanOrEqual(EXPORT_WINDOW_MS / 1000);
    // Another account is not affected.
    await enforceExportLimit(h.deps, randomUUID());
    h.advance(EXPORT_WINDOW_MS + 1);
    await enforceExportLimit(h.deps, h.userId);

    const failing: AccountDeps = {
      ...h.deps,
      limits: {
        hit: async () => {
          throw new Error("store down");
        },
        release: async () => undefined,
      },
    };
    const down = await enforceExportLimit(failing, h.userId).catch((err: unknown) => err);
    expect(down).toBeInstanceOf(AccountError);
    expect((down as AccountError).code).toBe("service_unavailable");
    expect((down as AccountError).status).toBe(503);
    expect((down as AccountError).retryAfterSeconds).toBe(30);
  });
});

describe("writing the archive", () => {
  test("the archive holds export.json and every image byte for byte, in chunks that are each awaited", async () => {
    const bytesA = randomBytes(200_000);
    const bytesB = Buffer.from("small-webp");
    const h = harness();
    h.images.push({ id: h.imageA, open: openerOf(fileOf(bytesA)) }, { id: h.imageB, open: openerOf(fileOf(bytesB)) });
    const plan = await buildExport(h.deps, h.userId, h.currentSession, h.now());
    const sink = memorySink();
    await writeExport(createZipWriter(sink.write), plan);
    expect(sink.overlapped).toBe(false);
    // Two hundred kilobytes do not fit in one read: the image went through several awaited writes.
    expect(sink.count).toBeGreaterThan(3);

    const files = unzipSync(sink.bytes());
    expect(Object.keys(files).sort()).toEqual(["export.json", `media/${h.imageA}.webp`, `media/${h.imageB}.webp`].sort());
    expect(Buffer.compare(Buffer.from(files[`media/${h.imageA}.webp`]!), bytesA)).toBe(0);
    expect(Buffer.compare(Buffer.from(files[`media/${h.imageB}.webp`]!), bytesB)).toBe(0);
    expect(strFromU8(files["export.json"]!)).toBe(JSON.stringify(expectedDocument(h), null, 2));
    expect(centralDirectory(sink.bytes()).map((entry) => [entry.name, entry.method])).toEqual([
      [`media/${h.imageA}.webp`, 0],
      [`media/${h.imageB}.webp`, 0],
      ["export.json", 8],
    ]);
  });

  test("an image whose file is gone is listed under missingMedia, and the archive still closes with the others", async () => {
    const bytesA = Buffer.from("still-there");
    const h = harness();
    h.images.push({ id: h.imageA, open: openerOf(fileOf(bytesA)) }, { id: h.imageB, open: openerOf(path.join(root, randomUUID(), "large.webp")) });
    const plan = await buildExport(h.deps, h.userId, h.currentSession, h.now());
    const sink = memorySink();
    await writeExport(createZipWriter(sink.write), plan);
    const files = unzipSync(sink.bytes());
    expect(Object.keys(files).sort()).toEqual(["export.json", `media/${h.imageA}.webp`].sort());
    expect(Buffer.compare(Buffer.from(files[`media/${h.imageA}.webp`]!), bytesA)).toBe(0);
    const json = ExportFormat.parse(JSON.parse(strFromU8(files["export.json"]!)));
    expect(json.missingMedia).toEqual([h.imageB]);
    // The post still names the entry the image would have had; missingMedia says why it is not there.
    expect(json.posts[0]!.media[1]!.file).toBe(`media/${h.imageB}.webp`);
    expect(plan.missingMedia).toEqual([h.imageB]);
  });

  /** A store with one image whose large variant holds `bytes`, read through the media module's checked open. */
  async function storeWith(id: string, bytes: Uint8Array) {
    const base = path.join(root, randomUUID());
    const files = createMediaFiles({ uploadsDir: path.join(base, "uploads"), storeDir: path.join(base, "store"), log: silent });
    await files.prepare();
    mkdirSync(files.store.imageDir(id), { recursive: true });
    writeFileSync(files.store.image(id, "large"), bytes);
    return files;
  }

  test("an image larger than a variant may be is refused by the checked open and listed under missingMedia like a missing one", async () => {
    const h = harness();
    const files = await storeWith(h.imageA, Buffer.from("planted"));
    // A sparse file of any size could be planted in the store; the checked open refuses anything over the variant limit.
    truncateSync(files.store.image(h.imageA, "large"), MAX_VARIANT_BYTES + 1);
    const kept = await storeWith(h.imageB, Buffer.from("fine"));
    h.images.push({ id: h.imageA, open: () => files.openImage(h.imageA, "large") }, { id: h.imageB, open: () => kept.openImage(h.imageB, "large") });
    const plan = await buildExport(h.deps, h.userId, h.currentSession, h.now());
    const sink = memorySink();
    await writeExport(createZipWriter(sink.write), plan);
    const archive = sink.bytes();
    expect(archive.length).toBeLessThan(MAX_VARIANT_BYTES);
    const unpacked = unzipSync(archive);
    expect(Object.keys(unpacked).sort()).toEqual(["export.json", `media/${h.imageB}.webp`].sort());
    expect(ExportFormat.parse(JSON.parse(strFromU8(unpacked["export.json"]!))).missingMedia).toEqual([h.imageA]);
  });

  test("a file that grows after the checked open is read only to the size the open measured", async () => {
    const h = harness();
    const original = randomBytes(150_000);
    const files = await storeWith(h.imageA, original);
    h.images.push({
      id: h.imageA,
      open: async () => {
        const stored = await files.openImage(h.imageA, "large");
        // Whatever lands in the file after the check is not the checked file's.
        appendFileSync(files.store.image(h.imageA, "large"), randomBytes(100_000));
        return stored;
      },
    });
    const sink = memorySink();
    await writeExport(createZipWriter(sink.write), await buildExport(h.deps, h.userId, h.currentSession, h.now()));
    const unpacked = unzipSync(sink.bytes());
    expect(Buffer.compare(Buffer.from(unpacked[`media/${h.imageA}.webp`]!), original)).toBe(0);
  });
});

describe("the zip writer", () => {
  test("entries come out in the order they were added: JSON pieces deflated as one text, files stored as they are", async () => {
    const stored = randomBytes(70_000);
    const first = JSON.stringify({ kind: "first", filler: "x".repeat(2_000) }, null, 2);
    const sink = memorySink();
    const writer = createZipWriter(sink.write);
    await writer.addJsonPieces("first.json", piecesOf(first.slice(0, 700), first.slice(700)));
    expect(await writer.addFile("files/stored.bin", openerOf(fileOf(stored)))).toBe(true);
    await writer.addJsonPieces("last.json", piecesOf('{ "kind": "last" }'));
    await writer.end();

    const files = unzipSync(sink.bytes());
    expect(Object.keys(files)).toEqual(["first.json", "files/stored.bin", "last.json"]);
    expect(strFromU8(files["first.json"]!)).toBe(first);
    expect(Buffer.compare(Buffer.from(files["files/stored.bin"]!), stored)).toBe(0);
    expect(strFromU8(files["last.json"]!)).toBe('{ "kind": "last" }');
    const directory = centralDirectory(sink.bytes());
    expect(directory.map((entry) => [entry.name, entry.method])).toEqual([
      ["first.json", 8],
      ["files/stored.bin", 0],
      ["last.json", 8],
    ]);
    // A plain archive has no ZIP64 field or record, and every entry streams its sizes after its data.
    expect(directory.map((entry) => entry.zip64)).toEqual([null, null, null]);
    expect(directory.every((entry) => entry.versionNeeded === 45 && (entry.flags & 0x0008) !== 0)).toBe(true);
    expect(endRecords(sink.bytes()).end64).toBeNull();
    expect(sink.overlapped).toBe(false);
  });

  test("a file the open refuses adds nothing and answers false; a zero-byte file is an entry without data", async () => {
    const dir = path.join(root, randomUUID());
    mkdirSync(dir, { recursive: true });
    const sink = memorySink();
    const writer = createZipWriter(sink.write);
    expect(await writer.addFile("missing.bin", openerOf(path.join(root, randomUUID(), "missing.webp")))).toBe(false);
    expect(await writer.addFile("dir.bin", openerOf(dir))).toBe(false);
    const empty = fakeFile(0);
    expect(await writer.addFile("empty.bin", empty.open)).toBe(true);
    expect(empty.state).toEqual({ chunks: 0, stopped: false, closed: true });
    await writer.addJsonPieces("only.json", piecesOf('{ "ok": true }'));
    await writer.end();
    const files = unzipSync(sink.bytes());
    expect(Object.keys(files)).toEqual(["empty.bin", "only.json"]);
    expect(files["empty.bin"]!.length).toBe(0);
    expect(centralDirectory(sink.bytes()).map((entry) => entry.name)).toEqual(["empty.bin", "only.json"]);
  });

  test("an empty archive is still a valid archive", async () => {
    const sink = memorySink();
    const writer = createZipWriter(sink.write);
    await writer.end();
    expect(unzipSync(sink.bytes())).toEqual({});
  });

  test("the JSON is fed to the deflate at most 64 KiB at a time, and the event loop turns between two feeds", async () => {
    const push = vi.spyOn(Deflate.prototype, "push");
    const chunks: Uint8Array[] = [];
    const writer = createZipWriter(async (chunk) => {
      chunks.push(Uint8Array.from(chunk));
    });
    let turns = 0;
    let running = true;
    const tick = () => {
      if (!running) return;
      turns += 1;
      setImmediate(tick);
    };
    setImmediate(tick);
    // One piece of 300 KiB and ten small ones.
    const big = "y".repeat(300 * 1024);
    let fed: number[];
    try {
      await writer.addJsonPieces("big.json", piecesOf(big, ...Array.from({ length: 10 }, (_, i) => `,${i}`)));
      await writer.end();
      // Read before the spy is restored, which forgets its calls.
      fed = push.mock.calls.map(([chunk]) => chunk.length);
    } finally {
      running = false;
      push.mockRestore();
    }
    expect(Math.max(...fed)).toBeLessThanOrEqual(KIB64);
    expect(fed.filter((length) => length > 0)).toHaveLength(5 + 10);
    expect(turns).toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(10);
    expect(strFromU8(unzipSync(Buffer.concat(chunks))["big.json"]!)).toBe(big + Array.from({ length: 10 }, (_, i) => `,${i}`).join(""));
  });

  test("forced ZIP64 on a small archive: it opens and gives back its bytes, and its records say what a ZIP64 reader needs", async () => {
    const stored = randomBytes(5_000);
    const sink = memorySink();
    const writer = createZipWriter(sink.write, { zip64: "always" });
    expect(await writer.addFile("a.bin", openerOf(fileOf(stored)))).toBe(true);
    await writer.addJsonPieces("b.json", piecesOf('{ "b": 1 }'));
    await writer.end();
    const archive = sink.bytes();

    const files = unzipSync(archive);
    expect(Object.keys(files)).toEqual(["a.bin", "b.json"]);
    expect(Buffer.compare(Buffer.from(files["a.bin"]!), stored)).toBe(0);
    expect(strFromU8(files["b.json"]!)).toBe('{ "b": 1 }');

    // Every 32-bit field reads 0xFFFFFFFF and the extra field holds the uncompressed size, the compressed size and the offset, in that order.
    const [a, b] = centralDirectory(archive);
    expect(a).toMatchObject({ name: "a.bin", compressed: 0xffffffff, size: 0xffffffff, offset: 0xffffffff, zip64: [5_000, 5_000, 0] });
    expect(b!.zip64![2]).toBe(30 + "a.bin".length + 5_000 + 24);
    expect(b!.zip64![0]).toBe(10);
    // The data descriptor after a.bin's bytes carries 8-byte sizes.
    const descriptor = 30 + "a.bin".length + 5_000;
    expect(archive.readUInt32LE(descriptor)).toBe(0x08074b50);
    expect([u64(archive, descriptor + 8), u64(archive, descriptor + 16)]).toEqual([5_000, 5_000]);

    const { end, locator, end64 } = endRecords(archive);
    const directoryOffset = a!.at;
    expect(end64).toEqual({
      at: archive.length - 22 - 20 - 56,
      recordSize: 44,
      versionMadeBy: 45,
      versionNeeded: 45,
      disk: 0,
      directoryDisk: 0,
      entriesHere: 2,
      entries: 2,
      size: end64!.at - directoryOffset,
      offset: directoryOffset,
    });
    expect(locator).toEqual({ disk: 0, offset: end64!.at, disks: 1 });
    expect(end).toEqual({ entriesHere: 0xffff, entries: 0xffff, size: 0xffffffff, offset: 0xffffffff, comment: 0 });
  });

  test("the writer turns to ZIP64 by itself once an offset passes 4 GiB", async () => {
    const start = TWO_32 - 100;
    const sink = memorySink();
    const writer = createZipWriter(sink.write, { startOffset: start });
    await writer.addFile("a.bin", openerOf(fileOf(Buffer.alloc(50, 1))));
    await writer.addFile("b.bin", openerOf(fileOf(Buffer.alloc(40, 2))));
    await writer.end();
    const archive = sink.bytes();

    const bOffset = start + 30 + 5 + 50 + 16;
    expect(bOffset).toBeGreaterThan(0xffffffff);
    const [a, b] = centralDirectory(archive, start);
    // a.bin starts below 4 GiB and needs nothing; b.bin's offset goes into the extra field alone.
    expect(a).toMatchObject({ name: "a.bin", compressed: 50, size: 50, offset: start, zip64: null });
    expect(b).toMatchObject({ name: "b.bin", compressed: 40, size: 40, offset: 0xffffffff, zip64: [bOffset] });
    // Neither entry reached 4 GiB, so both descriptors keep 4-byte sizes.
    expect(archive.readUInt32LE(30 + 5 + 50)).toBe(0x08074b50);
    expect(archive.readUInt32LE(30 + 5 + 50 + 16)).toBe(0x04034b50);

    const { end, locator, end64 } = endRecords(archive, start);
    expect(end64).toMatchObject({ entriesHere: 2, entries: 2, size: end64!.at - a!.at, offset: a!.at });
    expect(a!.at).toBeGreaterThan(0xffffffff);
    expect(locator).toEqual({ disk: 0, offset: end64!.at, disks: 1 });
    // Only the directory's offset overflows the classic record.
    expect(end).toEqual({ entriesHere: 2, entries: 2, size: end64!.at - a!.at, offset: 0xffffffff, comment: 0 });
  });

  test("an entry of more than 4 GiB is a ZIP64 entry by itself, without the archive being kept in memory", { timeout: 120_000 }, async () => {
    const huge = fakeFile(TWO_32 + 1);
    // Counts every byte and keeps only what is not the file's own data, with where it starts.
    const kept: { at: number; bytes: Uint8Array }[] = [];
    let written = 0;
    const writer = createZipWriter(async (chunk) => {
      if (chunk.buffer !== huge.chunk.buffer) kept.push({ at: written, bytes: Uint8Array.from(chunk) });
      written += chunk.length;
    });
    expect(await writer.addFile("huge.bin", huge.open)).toBe(true);
    await writer.addJsonPieces("after.json", piecesOf('{ "after": true }'));
    await writer.end();
    expect(huge.state).toEqual({ chunks: TWO_32 / KIB64 + 1, stopped: true, closed: true });

    // Everything after the file's data is kept together: its descriptor, the next entry, the directory and the end records.
    const dataEnd = 30 + "huge.bin".length + TWO_32 + 1;
    const tail = Buffer.concat(kept.filter((piece) => piece.at >= dataEnd).map((piece) => piece.bytes));
    expect(dataEnd + tail.length).toBe(written);
    expect(tail.readUInt32LE(0)).toBe(0x08074b50);
    expect([u64(tail, 8), u64(tail, 16)]).toEqual([TWO_32 + 1, TWO_32 + 1]);
    const [hugeEntry, after] = centralDirectory(tail, dataEnd);
    expect(hugeEntry).toMatchObject({ name: "huge.bin", compressed: 0xffffffff, size: 0xffffffff, offset: 0, zip64: [TWO_32 + 1, TWO_32 + 1] });
    expect(after).toMatchObject({ name: "after.json", offset: 0xffffffff, zip64: [dataEnd + 24] });
    const { end, end64 } = endRecords(tail, dataEnd);
    expect(end64).toMatchObject({ entries: 2, offset: hugeEntry!.at });
    expect(end).toMatchObject({ entries: 2, offset: 0xffffffff });
  });
});

describe("the export route", () => {
  /**
   * The account routes on their own, with the session and the logger a request would carry and an error
   * handler that renders AccountError as the app's does; everything else is a 500. The freshness and
   * session guards are passed through: http-account.test.ts covers them on the real app.
   */
  function app(h: Harness, log = silent) {
    const session: Session = {
      sessionId: randomBytes(32).toString("hex"),
      userId: h.userId,
      deviceId: randomUUID(),
      role: "user",
      onboarded: true,
      mfaEnabled: false,
      reauthAt: h.now(),
      // The route marks the current session by this, the id the list carries, and not by the token's hash above.
      handle: h.currentSession,
      factors: { email: h.now().getTime() },
      passkeyId: null,
    };
    const pass: MiddlewareHandler<AppEnv> = async (_c, next) => {
      await next();
    };
    const a = new Hono<AppEnv>();
    a.use(async (c, next) => {
      c.set("requestId", "test");
      c.set("log", log);
      c.set("session", session);
      c.set("authVia", "cookie");
      await next();
    });
    a.route("/api/account", accountRoutes(h.deps, pass, pass, pass));
    a.onError((err, c) => (err instanceof AccountError ? c.json({ error: { code: err.code } }, err.status) : c.json({ error: { code: "internal" } }, 500)));
    return a;
  }
  const exportOf = (a: Hono<AppEnv>) => a.request("/api/account/export", { method: "POST" });
  const errorCode = async (res: Response) => ((await res.json()) as { error: { code: string } }).error.code;
  const exported = (h: Harness) => h.events.filter((event) => event.type === "export_created").length;

  test("a complete export streams a valid archive with its headers and records export_created", async () => {
    const h = harness();
    const bytesA = randomBytes(300_000);
    h.images.push({ id: h.imageA, open: openerOf(fileOf(bytesA)) });
    const res = await exportOf(app(h));
    expect(res.status).toBe(200);
    expect(res.headers.get("content-type")).toBe("application/zip");
    expect(res.headers.get("content-disposition")).toBe(`attachment; filename="korbat-export-ada-${iso(T0).slice(0, 10)}.zip"`);
    expect(res.headers.get("cache-control")).toBe("no-store");
    const files = unzipSync(new Uint8Array(await res.arrayBuffer()));
    expect(Buffer.compare(Buffer.from(files[`media/${h.imageA}.webp`]!), bytesA)).toBe(0);
    expect(strFromU8(files["export.json"]!)).toBe(JSON.stringify(expectedDocument(h), null, 2));
    // Recorded once every chunk was taken, before the body ended.
    expect(h.events).toEqual([{ userId: h.userId, type: "export_created", metadata: undefined }]);
  });

  test("a failure before the first byte answers an error and gives the day's export back", async () => {
    const h = harness();
    const a = app(h);
    // The build fails: a pool timeout while the account is read.
    h.failures.exportAccount = 1;
    const failed = await exportOf(a);
    expect(failed.status).toBe(500);
    expect(await errorCode(failed)).toBe("internal");
    // The first image cannot even be opened: still nothing sent.
    h.images.push({
      id: h.imageA,
      open: async () => {
        throw new Error("too many open files");
      },
    });
    const unopened = await exportOf(a);
    expect(unopened.status).toBe(500);
    expect(exported(h)).toBe(0);
    h.images.length = 0;
    const ok = await exportOf(a);
    expect(ok.status).toBe(200);
    expect(Object.keys(unzipSync(new Uint8Array(await ok.arrayBuffer())))).toEqual(["export.json"]);
    expect(exported(h)).toBe(1);
    expect(await errorCode(await exportOf(a))).toBe("rate_limited");
  });

  test("a moderation read that fails before the first byte answers an error and gives the day's export back; the next export carries the member", async () => {
    const h = harness();
    const a = app(h);
    h.failures.exportFor = 1;
    const failed = await exportOf(a);
    expect(failed.status).toBe(500);
    expect(await errorCode(failed)).toBe("internal");
    expect(exported(h)).toBe(0);
    const ok = await exportOf(a);
    expect(ok.status).toBe(200);
    const json = JSON.parse(strFromU8(unzipSync(new Uint8Array(await ok.arrayBuffer()))["export.json"]!)) as { moderation: unknown };
    expect(json.moderation).toStrictEqual(expectedModeration(h));
    expect(exported(h)).toBe(1);
    expect(h.asked).toEqual([h.userId, h.userId]);
  });

  test("a limit store that cannot give the export back is logged, and the build's own error is answered", async () => {
    const h = harness();
    const lines: string[] = [];
    const log = pino({ level: "warn" }, new Writable({ write: (chunk: Buffer, _encoding, done) => (lines.push(chunk.toString("utf8")), done()) }));
    const store = new MemoryStore(() => h.now().getTime());
    h.deps.limits = {
      hit: (key, windowMs) => store.hit(key, windowMs),
      release: async () => {
        throw new Error("the store went away");
      },
    };
    h.failures.exportAccount = 1;
    const res = await exportOf(app(h, log));
    expect(res.status).toBe(500);
    expect(await errorCode(res)).toBe("internal");
    expect(lines.map((line) => (JSON.parse(line) as { level: number; msg: string }).level)).toEqual([40]);
    expect(lines[0]).toMatch(/could not be given back/);
  });

  test("an image that fails in the middle of its reading fails the response body, and the day's export stays spent", async () => {
    const h = harness();
    const failing = fakeFile(1_000_000, { failAfter: 3 });
    h.images.push({ id: h.imageA, open: failing.open });
    const a = app(h);
    const res = await exportOf(a);
    // The status went out with the first bytes; what follows can only end the body with an error, never cleanly.
    expect(res.status).toBe(200);
    await expect(res.arrayBuffer()).rejects.toThrow();
    expect(failing.state).toMatchObject({ chunks: 3, stopped: true, closed: true });
    expect(exported(h)).toBe(0);
    h.images.length = 0;
    expect(await errorCode(await exportOf(a))).toBe("rate_limited");
  });

  test("a client that goes away stops the file reads", async () => {
    const h = harness();
    // A hundred megabytes, read only as fast as the response is taken.
    const big = fakeFile(100 * 1024 * 1024);
    h.images.push({ id: h.imageA, open: big.open });
    const res = await exportOf(app(h));
    expect(res.status).toBe(200);
    const reader = res.body!.getReader();
    await reader.read();
    await reader.cancel();
    await vi.waitFor(() => expect(big.state).toMatchObject({ stopped: true, closed: true }));
    expect(big.state.chunks).toBeLessThan(10);
    expect(exported(h)).toBe(0);
  });
});

import { readFileSync } from "node:fs";

import { STAFF_USAGE, enrollSettings, migratorUrl, parseStaffArgs, revokeSettings, runStaffCommand, staffDatabaseUrls } from "../src/cli/staff";

const HASH_A = "ab".repeat(32);
const HASH_B = "0123456789abcdef".repeat(4);
const API_URL = "postgres://korbat_api:x@localhost:5432/korbat";
const AUTH_URL = "postgres://korbat_auth:x@localhost:5432/korbat";

/** The command's lines, each marked with the stream it went to. */
function capture() {
  const lines: string[] = [];
  return { lines, out: { log: (line: string) => lines.push(`out ${line}`), error: (line: string) => lines.push(`err ${line}`) } };
}

describe("staff.js arguments", () => {

    expect(STAFF_USAGE).toContain("revoke <email> <key id>");
    expect(STAFF_USAGE).toContain("revoke <email> all");
    // enroll runs as the migrator, in the migrate service; the usage says where.
    expect(STAFF_USAGE).toMatch(/run --rm migrate node dist\/staff\.js enroll/);
  });

  test("3d review L18 (walk): no command of the quarantine's and the release's usage runs past its column; each description starts at the 42nd character", () => {
    for (const line of CUSTODY_USAGE) {
      expect(line.length, line).toBeGreaterThan(41);
      expect(line.charAt(40), line).toBe(" ");
      expect(line.charAt(41), line).not.toBe(" ");
    }
    expect(STAFF_USAGE).toContain(`${"  release-leave <seal|refusal>".padEnd(41)}record a leave or an instruction to destroy`);
  });

  test("reads revoke with an email address and a key id or all, normalising both", () => {
    const id = "0f7b3c2e-4a1d-4c6b-9e8f-1a2b3c4d5e6f";

    expect(parseStaffArgs(["revoke", "mod@korbat.local", id.toUpperCase()])).toEqual({ command: "revoke", email: "mod@korbat.local", key: id });
    expect(() => parseStaffArgs(["revoke", "mod@korbat.local"])).toThrow(STAFF_USAGE);
    expect(() => parseStaffArgs(["revoke", "mod@korbat.local", id, "all"])).toThrow(STAFF_USAGE);
    expect(() => parseStaffArgs(["revoke", "moderator", "all"])).toThrow(`not an email address: moderator\n${STAFF_USAGE}`);
    for (const key of ["ALL", "every", "12", `${id}0`, id.replace(/-/g, "")]) {
      expect(() => parseStaffArgs(["revoke", "mod@korbat.local", key]), key).toThrow(`not a key id or all: ${key}`);
    }
  });

  test("reads enroll with one email address and keys with one or none, normalising the address", () => {
    expect(parseStaffArgs(["enroll", " Mod@Korbat.Local "])).toEqual({ command: "enroll", email: "mod@korbat.local" });
    expect(parseStaffArgs(["keys"])).toEqual({ command: "keys", email: null });
    expect(parseStaffArgs(["keys", "Mod@Korbat.Local"])).toEqual({ command: "keys", email: "mod@korbat.local" });
    expect(() => parseStaffArgs(["enroll"])).toThrow(STAFF_USAGE);
    expect(() => parseStaffArgs(["enroll", "a@b.io", "b@c.io"])).toThrow(STAFF_USAGE);
    expect(() => parseStaffArgs(["keys", "a@b.io", "b@c.io"])).toThrow(STAFF_USAGE);
    expect(() => parseStaffArgs(["enroll", "moderator"])).toThrow(`not an email address: moderator\n${STAFF_USAGE}`);
    expect(() => parseStaffArgs(["keys", "all"])).toThrow(`not an email address: all\n${STAFF_USAGE}`);
  });

  test("reads audit-head, and audit-verify with any number of kept places", () => {
    expect(parseStaffArgs(["audit-head"])).toEqual({ command: "audit-head" });
    expect(parseStaffArgs(["audit-verify"])).toEqual({ command: "audit-verify", kept: [] });
    expect(parseStaffArgs(["audit-verify", `12:${HASH_A}`, `3:${HASH_B}`])).toEqual({
      command: "audit-verify",

        { seq: 12, hash: HASH_A },
        { seq: 3, hash: HASH_B },

  test("prints the usage for no command, an unknown one or extra arguments", () => {

    expect(() => parseStaffArgs(["audit-head", `1:${HASH_A}`])).toThrow(STAFF_USAGE);

  test("refuses a kept place that is not <chain_seq>:<hash>, a positive place and a lower-case sha256", () => {

});

// audit-head and audit-verify need no server secret and no console configuration (3a design, section 7), so each reads
// only the database URLs it connects with, never the API's whole configuration.
describe("what each staff.js command reads of the environment", () => {
  test("audit-head reads DATABASE_URL_API alone, and audit-verify that and DATABASE_URL_AUTH", () => {
    expect(staffDatabaseUrls({ command: "audit-head" }, { DATABASE_URL_API: API_URL })).toEqual({ api: API_URL, auth: null });
    expect(staffDatabaseUrls({ command: "audit-verify", kept: [] }, { DATABASE_URL_API: API_URL, DATABASE_URL_AUTH: AUTH_URL })).toEqual({
      api: API_URL,
      auth: AUTH_URL,
    });
  });

  test("a setting the API's configuration would refuse, the console's included, changes nothing", () => {
    for (const extra of [
      // Not an origin as browsers send it (the final slash).
      { CONSOLE_ORIGIN: "https://console.example/" },
      // The console on the app's own origin.
      { APP_ORIGIN: "http://localhost:8081", CONSOLE_ORIGIN: "http://localhost:8081" },
      { CONSOLE_RP_ID: "not a domain" },
      // A secret too short, and production's rules over a development setup.
      { NODE_ENV: "production", AUTH_HMAC_KEY: "c2hvcnQ=", APP_ORIGIN: "http://localhost:8081" },
    ]) {
      const env = { DATABASE_URL_API: API_URL, DATABASE_URL_AUTH: AUTH_URL, ...extra };
      expect(staffDatabaseUrls({ command: "audit-verify", kept: [] }, env), JSON.stringify(extra)).toEqual({ api: API_URL, auth: AUTH_URL });
      expect(staffDatabaseUrls({ command: "audit-head" }, env), JSON.stringify(extra)).toEqual({ api: API_URL, auth: null });
    }
  });

  test("names the database URL that is missing or not a PostgreSQL URL, and no other setting", () => {
    const cases: [Parameters<typeof staffDatabaseUrls>[0], Record<string, string>, RegExp][] = [
      [{ command: "audit-head" }, {}, /DATABASE_URL_API/],
      [{ command: "audit-head" }, { DATABASE_URL_API: "mysql://korbat:x@localhost/korbat" }, /DATABASE_URL_API/],
      [{ command: "audit-verify", kept: [] }, { DATABASE_URL_API: API_URL }, /DATABASE_URL_AUTH/],
      [{ command: "audit-verify", kept: [] }, { DATABASE_URL_API: API_URL, DATABASE_URL_AUTH: "not a url" }, /DATABASE_URL_AUTH/],
    ];
    for (const [command, env, named] of cases) {
      let message = "";
      try {
        staffDatabaseUrls(command, env);
      } catch (err) {
        message = (err as Error).message;
      }
      expect(message, JSON.stringify(env)).toMatch(named);
      expect(message).toMatch(new RegExp(`^Invalid environment for ${command.command}:`));
      expect(message).not.toMatch(/APP_ORIGIN|REDIS_URL|AUTH_HMAC_KEY|SMTP_URL|CONSOLE_ORIGIN/);
    }
  });

  test("keys reads DATABASE_URL_AUTH for the keys and DATABASE_URL_API for the handles, and nothing else", () => {
    expect(staffDatabaseUrls({ command: "keys", email: null }, { DATABASE_URL_API: API_URL, DATABASE_URL_AUTH: AUTH_URL, CONSOLE_ORIGIN: "not an origin" })).toEqual({
      api: API_URL,

    expect(() => staffDatabaseUrls({ command: "keys", email: "a@b.io" }, { DATABASE_URL_API: API_URL })).toThrow(/^Invalid environment for keys:[\s\S]*DATABASE_URL_AUTH/);
  });

  test("run with a database URL missing, it names it and answers 1", async () => {
    const { lines, out } = capture();
    expect(await runStaffCommand(["audit-verify"], { DATABASE_URL_API: API_URL }, out)).toBe(1);
    expect(lines).toHaveLength(1);
    expect(lines[0]).toMatch(/^err Invalid environment for audit-verify:/);
    expect(lines[0]).toContain("DATABASE_URL_AUTH");
    expect(lines[0]).not.toMatch(/APP_ORIGIN|REDIS_URL|AUTH_HMAC_KEY/);
  });
});

// enroll runs in the migrate service as the migrator (3a design, section 7): it reads the migrator's database URL and the
// console's origin and relying party ID, which Compose gives that service, and nothing of the API's configuration.
describe("what staff.js enroll reads of the environment", () => {
  const MIGRATE_URL = "postgres://korbat_migrate:x@localhost:5432/korbat";

      migrate: MIGRATE_URL,

  });

      // The console on the app's own hostname is refused by the API's rules in production, not here.

      NODE_ENV: "production",

  });

      expect(() => enrollSettings(env), JSON.stringify(env)).toThrow(/CONSOLE_ORIGIN is not set: the staff console is off, so no enrolment link can be issued/);

  test("names the setting that is wrong, and no other", () => {
    const cases: [Record<string, string>, RegExp][] = [
      [{ CONSOLE_ORIGIN: "http://localhost:8090" }, /DATABASE_URL_MIGRATE/],
      [{ DATABASE_URL_MIGRATE: "mysql://x@localhost/k", CONSOLE_ORIGIN: "http://localhost:8090" }, /DATABASE_URL_MIGRATE/],
      // Not an origin as browsers send it: the staff gate would refuse every write the console makes.
      [{ DATABASE_URL_MIGRATE: MIGRATE_URL, CONSOLE_ORIGIN: "http://localhost:8090/" }, /CONSOLE_ORIGIN/],
      [{ DATABASE_URL_MIGRATE: MIGRATE_URL, CONSOLE_ORIGIN: "http://localhost:8090", CONSOLE_RP_ID: "http://localhost" }, /CONSOLE_RP_ID/],
    ];
    for (const [env, named] of cases) {
      let message = "";
      try {
        enrollSettings(env);
      } catch (err) {
        message = (err as Error).message;
      }
      expect(message, JSON.stringify(env)).toMatch(named);
      expect(message).toMatch(/^Invalid environment for enroll:/);
      expect(message).not.toMatch(/APP_ORIGIN|REDIS_URL|AUTH_HMAC_KEY|SMTP_URL|DATABASE_URL_API|DATABASE_URL_AUTH/);
    }
  });

  test("run while CONSOLE_ORIGIN is unset, it says so, answers 1 and connects to nothing", async () => {
    const { lines, out } = capture();
    // Nothing listens on port 1: a connection attempt would fail with another message, or hang.
    const started = Date.now();
    expect(await runStaffCommand(["enroll", "mod@korbat.local"], { DATABASE_URL_MIGRATE: "postgres://korbat_migrate:x@127.0.0.1:1/korbat" }, out)).toBe(1);
    expect(Date.now() - started).toBeLessThan(2_000);
    expect(lines).toHaveLength(1);
    expect(lines[0]).toMatch(/^err .*CONSOLE_ORIGIN is not set/);
  });
});

// revoke runs like grant-role, in the api service (3a design, section 7): it revokes on the auth role and mails the key's

    }

    expect(STAFF_USAGE).not.toContain("account-facts");
    for (const words of ["records [--verify]", "notification-facts <record>", "notification-sent <record>", "production-account <order>", "address-check --handle <handle> < address", "handover-list <seal action>", "handover-record <production>", "handover-destroyed <production>"]) {

    }
  });

  test("3f's review: alert-test, with or without --on-call, and nothing else; and every runbook step that publishes a test names the staff.js command that does", () => {
    expect(STAFF_USAGE).toContain("  alert-test [--on-call] ");
    expect(parseStaffArgs(["alert-test"])).toEqual({ command: "alert-test", onCall: false });
    expect(parseStaffArgs(["alert-test", "--on-call"])).toEqual({ command: "alert-test", onCall: true });
    for (const args of [["alert-test", "--all"], ["alert-test", "--on-call", "--on-call"]]) expect(() => parseStaffArgs(args), args.join(" ")).toThrow(STAFF_USAGE);
    // Nobody on call can publish: the phones only subscribe. A step that asks for a test push names the command, and the
    // command is one the usage lists.
    const readme = readFileSync(path.resolve(import.meta.dirname, "..", "..", "..", "README.md"), "utf8");
    const steps = readme.split(String.fromCharCode(10)).filter((line) => /publish(es)? a test/.test(line));
    expect(steps.length).toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(2);
    for (const step of steps) {
      const named = [...step.matchAll(/staff\.js ([a-z-]+)/g)].map((match) => match[1]!);
      expect(named.length, step).toBeGreaterThan(0);

    }

  test("reads link and unlink with a staff address and a personal handle, with or without its at sign, in lower case", () => {

    }
  });

  test("reads limits with exactly five whole numbers from 1, in the order of the usage", () => {
    expect(parseStaffArgs(["limits", "60", "300", "400", "50", "10"])).toEqual({
      command: "limits",
      limits: { decisionsPerHour: 60, decisionsPerDay: 300, caseOpensPerDay: 400, findingsPerDay: 50, revealsPerDay: 10 },

    expect(() => parseStaffArgs(["limits", "60", "300", "400", "50", "10", "5"])).toThrow(STAFF_USAGE);
    for (const number of ["0", "-1", "1.5", "1e3", "ten", "", " 5", "05", "12345678"]) {
      expect(() => parseStaffArgs(["limits", "60", "300", number, "50", "10"]), JSON.stringify(number)).toThrow(`not a limit: ${number}`);
    }
  });

  test("reads text-verify without arguments, the record commands with what they name and their flags, and access-request with a handle or an address", () => {
    expect(parseStaffArgs(["text-verify"])).toEqual({ command: "text-verify" });
    expect(() => parseStaffArgs(["text-verify", "now"])).toThrow(STAFF_USAGE);
    // 3f Task 5: account-facts is gone; notification-facts names a record.
    expect(() => parseStaffArgs(["account-facts", "@Ada", CASE])).toThrow("unknown command: account-facts");
    expect(parseStaffArgs(["notification-facts", CASE])).toEqual({ command: "record", record: { command: "notification-facts", target: CASE, positional: [], flags: new Map() } });
    const sent = parseStaffArgs(["notification-sent", CASE, "--duty", "dsa18_1", "--duty", "tco14_5", "--kinds", "handle,address"]);
    expect(sent).toMatchObject({ command: "record", record: { command: "notification-sent", target: CASE } });
    expect((sent as { record: { flags: Map<string, string[]> } }).record.flags.get("--duty")).toEqual(["dsa18_1", "tco14_5"]);
    expect(parseStaffArgs(["records", "--verify"])).toMatchObject({ command: "record", record: { command: "records", target: null } });
    expect(() => parseStaffArgs(["records", CASE])).toThrow(/records: takes no/);
    expect(() => parseStaffArgs(["notification-facts"])).toThrow(/notification-facts: name the record/);
    expect(() => parseStaffArgs(["handover-list", "--instrument"])).toThrow(/needs a value/);
    // An at sign in front is a handle's; one inside is an address's.
    expect(parseStaffArgs(["access-request", "@Ada"])).toEqual({ command: "access-request", who: { handle: "ada" } });
    expect(parseStaffArgs(["access-request", "ada"])).toEqual({ command: "access-request", who: { handle: "ada" } });
    expect(parseStaffArgs(["access-request", " Ada@Korbat.Local "])).toEqual({ command: "access-request", who: { email: "ada@korbat.local" } });
    expect(() => parseStaffArgs(["access-request"])).toThrow(STAFF_USAGE);
    expect(() => parseStaffArgs(["access-request", "ada", "bob"])).toThrow(STAFF_USAGE);
    expect(() => parseStaffArgs(["access-request", "ada lovelace"])).toThrow("not a handle: ada lovelace");
  });

  test("text-verify reads DATABASE_URL_API alone; link, unlink and limits the migrator's URL alone", () => {
    expect(staffDatabaseUrls({ command: "text-verify" }, { DATABASE_URL_API: API_URL })).toEqual({ api: API_URL, auth: null });
    expect(() => staffDatabaseUrls({ command: "text-verify" }, { DATABASE_URL_AUTH: AUTH_URL })).toThrow(/DATABASE_URL_API/);
    expect(migratorUrl("limits", { DATABASE_URL_MIGRATE: MIGRATE_URL, CONSOLE_ORIGIN: "not an origin", SMTP_URL: "nonsense" })).toBe(MIGRATE_URL);
    expect(() => migratorUrl("link", { DATABASE_URL_API: API_URL })).toThrow(/Invalid environment for link:[^]*DATABASE_URL_MIGRATE/);
  });

  test("run in the wrong service, each says which URL it lacks, answers 1 and connects to nothing", async () => {
    for (const args of [["link", "mod@korbat.local", "ada"], ["unlink", "mod@korbat.local", "ada"], ["limits", "60", "300", "400", "50", "10"], ["records"], ["notification-facts", CASE]]) {
      const { lines, out } = capture();
      expect(await runStaffCommand(args, { DATABASE_URL_API: API_URL, DATABASE_URL_AUTH: AUTH_URL }, out), args[0]).toBe(1);
      expect(lines, args[0]).toHaveLength(1);
      expect(lines[0], args[0]).toMatch(new RegExp(`^err Invalid environment for ${args[0]}:`));
      expect(lines[0], args[0]).toContain("DATABASE_URL_MIGRATE");
    }
    // access-request for an address reads the API's whole configuration, and refuses with what is missing of it.
    const { lines, out } = capture();
    expect(await runStaffCommand(["access-request", "ada@korbat.local"], { DATABASE_URL_MIGRATE: MIGRATE_URL }, out)).toBe(1);
    expect(lines).toHaveLength(1);
    expect(lines[0]).toMatch(/^err /);
    expect(lines[0]).toContain("DATABASE_URL_API");
    // 3f Task 5: for a handle it runs in the migrate service, which holds the migrator's URL and APP_ORIGIN.
    const handle = capture();
    expect(await runStaffCommand(["access-request", "@ada"], { DATABASE_URL_API: API_URL, DATABASE_URL_AUTH: AUTH_URL }, handle.out)).toBe(1);
    expect(handle.lines).toEqual(["err access-request: a handle's draft runs in the migrate service, which holds DATABASE_URL_MIGRATE and APP_ORIGIN; nothing was drafted"]);
    const noOrigin = capture();
    expect(await runStaffCommand(["access-request", "@ada"], { DATABASE_URL_MIGRATE: MIGRATE_URL }, noOrigin.out)).toBe(1);
    expect(noOrigin.lines).toEqual(handle.lines);
  });
});

  async function staffBrowser(role: "moderator" | "admin") {

    await apiDb.insert(profiles).values({ id: user.id, handle: `s_${randomUUID().slice(0, 8)}`, displayName: "Staff" });
    staffIds.push(user.id);
    const soft = new SoftAuthenticator();
    const link = await issueEnrolment(migrateDb, user.id);
    const enrolled = await enrolKey({ deps: auth.deps, ctx: { ipHash: randomToken(), userAgent: undefined } }, soft, link.token);
    let counter = 0;
    const assert = (challenge: string) => soft.get({ credentialId: enrolled.credentialId, rpId: TEST_CONSOLE_RP_ID, challenge, origin: TEST_CONSOLE_ORIGIN, flags: DEVICE_BOUND, counter: ++counter });
    const b = consoleBrowser();
    const options = await b.fetch("/api/staff/signin/options", { method: "POST" });
    expect(options.status, await options.clone().text()).toBe(200);
    const { challenge } = ((await options.json()) as { options: { challenge: string } }).options;
    const signedIn = await b.fetch("/api/staff/signin/verify", { json: { response: assert(challenge) } });
    expect(signedIn.status, await signedIn.clone().text()).toBe(200);
    return { id: user.id, keyId: enrolled.key.id, role, b, assert };
  }
  type Staff = typeof moderator;

  /** A confirmed decision on the case over HTTP; answers the decision's id. */
  async function decide(s: Staff, caseId: string, input: DecisionInput): Promise<string> {
    const params = await decisionParams(apiDb, s, caseId, input);
    const request = { action: "case_decided" as const, target: { type: "case" as const, id: caseId }, params: params as CaseDecidedParams };
    const options = await s.b.fetch("/api/staff/step-up/options", { json: request, headers: MARKED });
    expect(options.status, await options.clone().text()).toBe(200);
    const stepUp: AuthenticationResponseJSON = s.assert(StaffStepUpOptionsResponse.parse(await options.json()).options.challenge);
    const view = await parsed(await s.b.fetch(`/api/staff/cases/${caseId}/decisions`, { json: { ...params, stepUp }, headers: MARKED }), 201, CaseView);
    await settle();
    return view.decisions.at(-1)!.id;
  }

  /**
   * An image uploaded over HTTP and accepted by the stand-in worker with the test model's score, then posted: the post's
   * answer comes first, and the program's step runs after its commit, which settle waits for.
   */
  async function publish(author: Awaited<ReturnType<typeof signUp>>, score: number, model = R1_TEST_MODEL) {
    const sent = await author.b.fetch("/api/media", { raw: { type: "image/jpeg", body: BYTES.jpeg } });
    expect(sent.status).toBe(202);
    const { id } = UploadResponse.parse(await sent.json());
    mediaIds.push(id);
    worker.ready(id, { width: 1200, height: 800 }, { model, score });
    expect(MediaStatusResponse.parse(await (await author.b.fetch(`/api/media/${id}`)).json()).status).toBe("ready");
    const created = await author.b.fetch("/api/posts", { json: { body: "a photo", media: [{ id, alt: "an image" }] } });
    expect(created.status, await created.clone().text()).toBe(201);
    const post = PostView.parse(await created.json());
    await settle();
    return { postId: post.id, mediaId: id };
  }

  /** What the program left on an image: its signal, the decision and its case, and the image's state. */
  async function programOn(mediaId: string) {
    const [row] = await apiDb.execute<{ handled: string | null; decision_id: string | null; case_id: string | null; state: string }>(sql`
      select s.handled, s.decision_id, i.case_id, m.moderation_state::text as state
        from post_media m left join automated_signals s on s.media_id = m.id left join intake_items i on i.id = s.intake_item_id
       where m.id = ${mediaId}::uuid`);
    return row!;
  }

  /** The case's row in the queue, read page by page in the queue's order, and the rows of its lane before it. */
  async function queueRowOf(caseId: string) {
    const rows: QueuePage["cases"] = [];
    let cursor: string | null = null;
    for (let page = 0; page < 50; page++) {
      const answer: QueuePage = await parsed(await moderator.b.fetch(`/api/staff/queue${cursor === null ? "" : `?cursor=${encodeURIComponent(cursor)}`}`), 200, QueuePage);
      rows.push(...answer.cases);
      const found = rows.find((row) => row.id === caseId);
      if (found) return { row: found, before: rows.slice(0, rows.indexOf(found)).filter((row) => row.lane === found.lane) };
      if (answer.nextCursor === null) break;
      cursor = answer.nextCursor;
    }
    throw new Error(`case ${caseId} is not in the queue`);
  }

  let program: { author: Awaited<ReturnType<typeof signUp>>; postId: string; mediaId: string; decisionId: string; caseId: string };

  test("a scored image on a new post: after the post's commit a program withholds it, interim and fully automated, with its statement and its mail", async () => {
    const author = await signUp();
    const { postId, mediaId } = await publish(author, 1);
    const left = await programOn(mediaId);
    expect([left.handled, left.state]).toEqual(["measure", "withheld"]);
    const [decision] = await apiDb.execute<{ kind: string; decided_by: string | null; automated_detection: boolean; automated_decision: string; source: string; rule_id: string; redress_version: number }>(
      sql`select kind::text, decided_by, automated_detection, automated_decision, source::text, rule_id, redress_version from decisions where id = ${left.decision_id!}::uuid`,
    );
    expect({ ...decision! }).toEqual({ kind: "interim", decided_by: null, automated_detection: true, automated_decision: "fully", source: "own_initiative", rule_id: "R1", redress_version: 4 });
    program = { author, postId, mediaId, decisionId: left.decision_id!, caseId: left.case_id! };

    // The author's list marks it as a program's, and its screen offers "Ask for a person".
    const cases = await parsed(await author.b.fetch("/api/moderation/cases"), 200, AuthorCasesPage);
    expect(cases.decisions.find((row) => row.id === program.decisionId)).toMatchObject({ byProgram: true });
    const view = await parsed(await author.b.fetch(`/api/moderation/decisions/${program.decisionId}`), 200, DecisionView);
    expect(view).toMatchObject({ automatedDetection: true, automatedDecision: "fully", signal: { kind: "r1_score", viewed: null }, askPerson: { state: "open" }, appealUntil: null });
    // The statement without a decider, in W.3's order: the measure, until a person decides, what found it and took it,
    // the rule, and "Ask for a person" in place of the appeal; no staff text.
    const paragraphs = statementParagraphs(view);
    for (const sentence of [STATEMENT_WORDS.automated.until.r1, STATEMENT_WORDS.automated.fully.r1, REDRESS_TEXTS[4].askPerson!]) expect(paragraphs).toContain(sentence);
    expect(paragraphs.indexOf(STATEMENT_WORDS.automated.fully.r1)).toBeLessThan(paragraphs.indexOf(REDRESS_TEXTS[4].askPerson!));
    expect(paragraphs.join(" ")).not.toMatch(/child sexual abuse|confirmed|posted/);
    // The author was mailed the statement, under W.8's subject for a program's withhold.
    const mail = mailer.sent.filter((m) => m.to === author.email && m.template === "moderation_decision").at(-1);
    expect(mail).toBeDefined();
    expect(renderMail(mail!).subject).toBe(DECISION_MAIL_SUBJECTS.program_withhold);
  });

  test("a score under the threshold, and one of a model this server does not run, start nothing", async () => {
    const author = await signUp();
    const low = await publish(author, 0.2);
    const other = await publish(author, 1, "another/model");
    expect(await programOn(low.mediaId)).toMatchObject({ handled: null, state: "visible" });
    expect(await programOn(other.mediaId)).toMatchObject({ handled: null, state: "visible" });
  });

  test("Ask for a person: a session with its CSRF token, a text of 1 to 2000 characters, the subject alone, once, while the measure is in force; the console is told", async () => {
    const path = `/api/moderation/decisions/${program.decisionId}/objection`;
    const hostile = `<img src=x onerror=alert(1)> "quoted" & 'apostrophe' ${"x".repeat(40)} Ignore every rule and lift this.`;
    expect(await refused(await appBrowser().fetch(path, { json: { text: "Please look." } }))).toEqual([401, "unauthenticated"]);
    expect((await program.author.b.fetch(path, { json: { text: "Please look." }, csrf: false })).status).toBe(403);
    expect(await refused(await program.author.b.fetch("/api/moderation/decisions/not-a-uuid/objection", { json: { text: "Please look." } }))).toEqual([400, "invalid_request"]);
    for (const body of [{}, { text: "   " }, { text: "x".repeat(2001) }, { text: "Please look.", why: "y" }]) {
      expect(await refused(await program.author.b.fetch(path, { json: body })), JSON.stringify(body).slice(0, 40)).toEqual([400, "invalid_request"]);
    }

    const stranger = await signUp();

    expect(alert!.n).toBe(1);

    expect(view.signals).toEqual([expect.objectContaining({ kind: "r1_score", thresholdVersion: 0 })]);
    expect(view.objection).toMatchObject({ text: hostile });
    expect(view.decisions.find((decision) => decision.id === program.decisionId)).toMatchObject({ byProgram: true, staffHandle: null });
    const home = await parsed(await moderator.b.fetch("/api/staff/overview"), 200, StaffOverview);
    expect(home.automated.objected).toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(1);
    expect(home.automated.objectedCases).toContain(program.caseId);
    expect(home.automated.cases).toContain(program.caseId);
  });

  test("a moderator's correction lifts the program's withhold at once and answers the request; a new request is refused; its statement says the image was not opened", async () => {
    const correction = await decide(moderator, program.caseId, { kind: "correction", outcome: "reversed", reviewsDecisionId: program.decisionId, actions: [act("restore_media", program.mediaId)] });
    expect((await programOn(program.mediaId)).state).toBe("visible");
    const view = await parsed(await program.author.b.fetch(`/api/moderation/decisions/${program.decisionId}`), 200, DecisionView);
    expect(view.askPerson).toMatchObject({ state: "decided", decisionId: correction });
    expect(await refused(await program.author.b.fetch(`/api/moderation/decisions/${program.decisionId}/objection`, { json: { text: "Once more." } }))).toEqual([422, "objection_not_open"]);
    // The correction is a person's: it records what found the item, and no image_viewed row of the moderator stands.
    const corrected = await parsed(await program.author.b.fetch(`/api/moderation/decisions/${correction}`), 200, DecisionView);
    expect(corrected).toMatchObject({ automatedDetection: true, automatedDecision: "not_automated", signal: { kind: "r1_score", viewed: false }, askPerson: null });
    const { row } = await queueRowOf(program.caseId).catch(() => ({ row: null }));
    if (row !== null) expect(row).toMatchObject({ takenByProgram: false, objected: false });
  });

  test("the sweep takes an image whose step never ran, and the daily alert follows a request that waited past the target, once in 24 hours", async () => {
    const author = await signUp();
    // An image scored and posted straight to the tables, so createPost never handed it to the step.
    const sent = await author.b.fetch("/api/media", { raw: { type: "image/jpeg", body: BYTES.jpeg } });
    const { id } = UploadResponse.parse(await sent.json());
    mediaIds.push(id);

    expect(MediaStatusResponse.parse(await (await author.b.fetch(`/api/media/${id}`)).json()).status).toBe("ready");
    // Written now: the sweep reads the posts of the last SWEEP_HOURS hours.
    const postId = await newPostRow(apiDb, author.id, { createdAt: sql`now()` });
    await apiDb.execute(sql`update post_media set post_id = ${postId}::uuid, position = 0, alt_text = 'an image' where id = ${id}::uuid`);
    expect((await programOn(id)).handled).toBeNull();

    // The sweep's round as the job runs it, on the module's dependencies with the same settings.
    const deps = automationDeps(apiDb);

    await deps.background.settle();
    expect(swept.signalled).toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(1);
    const taken = await programOn(id);
    expect([taken.handled, taken.state]).toEqual(["measure", "withheld"]);

    await parsed(await author.b.fetch(`/api/moderation/decisions/${taken.decision_id}/objection`, { json: { text: "Please have a person look." } }), 201, DecisionView);

    expect((await sweepRound(deps)).waiting).toBe(false);

    // The request is not a limit until it is older than unansweredHours: the program still acts.
    expect(AUTOMATION_RULES.objectionTargetHours + 1).toBeLessThan(AUTOMATION_RULES.unansweredHours);
  });

  test("this file left no row behind: the tables it writes hold what they held before it", async () => {

    await removeFixtures(migrateDb, [...profileIds, ...staffIds]);
    await removeAutomation(migrateDb, startedAt, mediaIds);

    staffIds.length = 0;

 * 4), against the real database: the moderation module's recordIntake as the routes of a later task will call it, as
 * korbat_api. A test with one session runs inside a transaction that is rolled back (the module's own transaction is
 * then a savepoint of it); the one test with two sessions commits, and removes what it committed in a `finally`. The
 * runs the module makes again after a deadlock, a lock timeout or a closed case are tested without a database
 * (test/moderation-retry.test.ts) and, for a case a decision closed under an intake, with one (moderation-races.test.ts).

  /** The snapshots of these cases as stored, each with the digest recomputed from its own columns. */
  async function snapshots(tx: DbTx, caseIds: readonly string[]) {
    const iso = (column: string) => sql.raw(`to_char(${column} at time zone 'UTC', 'YYYY-MM-DD"T"HH24:MI:SS.MS"Z"')`);
    const rows = await tx.execute<Record<string, unknown> & { case_id: string; digest: string }>(sql`
      select s.case_id, s.target_type, s.target_id, ${iso("s.taken_at")} as taken, s.author_handle, s.post_state, ${iso("s.post_created_at")} as created, s.reply_to_id, s.quote_of_id, s.body, s.media,
             s.display_name, s.bio, s.handle, s.salt, s.digest
        from evidence_snapshots s where s.case_id = any(${uuids(caseIds)}) order by s.taken_at, s.id`);
    return Promise.all(
      rows.map(async (row) => {
        const input = {
          salt: row.salt,
          targetType: row.target_type,
          targetId: row.target_id,
          takenAt: row.taken,
          authorHandle: row.author_handle,
          postState: row.post_state,

          replyToId: row.reply_to_id,

          bio: row.bio,
          handle: row.handle,

          const [stored] = await tx.execute<{ lookup_hash: string; reporter_id: string | null; channel: string }>(sql`select lookup_hash, reporter_id, channel from intakes where id = ${recorded.intakeId}::uuid`);
          expect({ ...stored! }).toEqual({ lookup_hash: createHash("sha256").update(recorded.token!).digest("hex"), reporter_id: null, channel: "signed_out" });
        }
        // Signed-out notices are never merged: each is an item of its own in the case.
        const [items] = await tx.execute<{ n: number }>(sql`select count(*)::int as n from intake_items where target_id = ${postId}::uuid`);
        expect(items!.n).toBe(2);

    test("a suspect report about a post that quotes another adds an item for the quoted post, once, at the lowest position that quotes it plus 10, and one level deep", async () => {
      await rolledBack(apiDb, async (tx) => {

        const [alone, quotingOne, quotingTwo] = [await post(), await post({ quoteOfId: quoted }), await post({ quoteOfId: quoted })];
        // A post that the notice names itself and that another named post quotes gets no second item.
        const named = await post();
        const quotingNamed = await post({ quoteOfId: named });
        const targets = [aPost(alone, 1), aPost(quotingTwo, 5), aPost(quotingOne, 2), aPost(named, 3), aPost(quotingNamed, 4)];

        const recorded = await intake(tx, ground.csam(), targets);

        expect(recorded.items.map((item) => [item.position, item.targetId])).toEqual([[1, alone], [2, quotingOne], [3, named], [4, quotingNamed], [5, quotingTwo], [12, quoted]]);

        expect(await pgError(tx.execute(sql`set constraints public.intake_items_quote immediate`))).toBeNull();
        await tx.execute(sql`set constraints public.intake_items_quote deferred`);

        expect(await snapshots(tx, recorded.items.map((item) => item.caseId!))).toHaveLength(6);

        // A finding citing R2 is suspect too; a report under any other rule adds nothing.

        expect((await intake(tx, ground.rule((await profile(tx)).id, "R5"), aPost(quotingOne))).items.map((item) => item.position)).toEqual([1]);
      });

        const rows = await tx.execute<Record<string, unknown>>(sql`select position, target_id, named_handle, outcome, case_id is null as no_case from intake_items where intake_id = ${recorded.intakeId}::uuid order by position`);

          const [row] = await apiDb.execute<{ state: string }>(sql`select state from posts where id = ${postId}::uuid`);

  test("this file left no row behind: the tables it writes hold what they held before it", async () => {

// Most tests here issue dozens of statements, each a round trip, and several hold a transaction open across them: on a
// loaded machine that takes longer than the five seconds a test gets by default.
vi.setConfig({ testTimeout: 30_000 });

/** The public tables migration 0015 creates, and what the API role holds on each beside SELECT. */
const APPEND_ONLY = ["cases", "decision_actions", "appeals", "staff_texts", "evidence_snapshots", "case_access_log", "media_holds"];
const COLUMN_UPDATES: Record<string, string[]> = {
