    const unmailed = renderTemplate("head_unmailed", { day: "2026-10-18T00:00:00.000Z", now: NOW });
    expect(unmailed.subject).toBe("korbat: The keeper did not get a daily value");
    expect(paragraphs(unmailed.text)).toEqual([
      "The audit log's value of 2026-10-18 was published, and its mail to the keeper never went out.",
      "The operator checks the mail relay and HEAD_KEEPER_MAIL (staff.js automation-status prints the last mail's outcome). The keeper copies that day's value from /transparency and notes that its mail did not come.",
      LAST_STAFF,
    ]);
    linkless(unmailed);
    expect(TICK_MAILED_KINDS).toContain("head_unmailed");
  });

  test("head_published: to the keeper alone, the day in the subject, the value, the place, the hash and whether a timestamp is stored, pinned", () => {
    const r = renderTemplate("head_published", { day: "2026-10-18", value: VALUE, seq: "42", hash: HASH, witnessed: "stored" });
    expect(r.subject).toBe("korbat: the audit log's value of 2026-10-18");
    expect(paragraphs(r.text)).toEqual([
      `Value: ${VALUE}. Place: 42. Hash: ${HASH}. Outside timestamp: stored.`,
      "Keep this mail. The value is public; the place and the hash are not: they let you check the value, and they go to you alone.",
      LAST_STAFF,
    ]);
    linkless(r);
    expect(paragraphs(renderTemplate("head_published", { day: "2026-10-18", value: VALUE, seq: "0", hash: "0".repeat(64), witnessed: "none" }).text)[0]).toBe(
      `Value: ${VALUE}. Place: 0. Hash: ${"0".repeat(64)}. Outside timestamp: none.`,
    );
    // Nothing but a day, a value of the head's form, a place and a hash: a mail never carries anything else.
    for (const [name, bad] of [["day", "18 October"], ["value", "x".repeat(64)], ["seq", "-1"], ["hash", "an entry"], ["witnessed", "yes"]] as const) {
      expect(() => renderTemplate("head_published", { day: "2026-10-18", value: VALUE, seq: "42", hash: HASH, witnessed: "none", [name]: bad }), name).toThrow(new RegExp(name));
    }
  });
});

describe("3d Task 7: the known material's mails (W.7, W.8)", () => {

    expect(r.text).not.toMatch(/https?:|www[.]|:[/][/]/);
    expect(r.html).not.toMatch(/<img|<a |href=|https?:/);
    expect(() => renderTemplate("upload_refused", {})).toThrow(/notice/);
  });

  test("upload_hold_lifted: the end's paragraph and the same last paragraph without the objection", () => {
    const ended = UPLOAD_NOTICE.ended.noReport("2026-10-18 09:00 UTC");
    const r = renderTemplate("upload_hold_lifted", { notice: ended });
    expect(r.subject).toBe("korbat lifted the hold on an image you uploaded");
    expect(paragraphs(r.text)).toEqual([ended, UPLOAD_NOTICE.mailReadLifted, LAST_USER]);
    expect(UPLOAD_NOTICE.mailReadLifted).not.toContain("object");
    expect(r.html).not.toMatch(/<img|<a |href=|https?:/);
  });

  test("matcher_down and hold_ended_unreported: their pushes' sentences with the line of what to do, every number from a constant, counts and times only", () => {
    const facts = { since: "2026-10-19T11:30:00.000Z", count: "3", refusalsCapped: "21" };
    const r = renderTemplate("matcher_down", { ...facts, now: NOW });
    const push = renderAlert("matcher_down", { since: facts.since, count: 3, refusalsCapped: 21 }, new Date(NOW));
    expect(r.subject).toBe("korbat: The comparison of uploads needs the operator");
    expect(paragraphs(r.text)).toEqual([push.sentence, push.todo, LAST_STAFF]);
    expect(push.sentence).toBe(`Uploads are not being compared as usual. 3 are unchecked, the oldest since 11:30 UTC. 21 matched within an hour over the limit of ${AUTOMATION_RULES.refusalsPerHour} refusals and were not refused.`);
    expect(push.todo).toContain(`checked again for ${AUTOMATION_RULES.matchRetryHours} hours`);
    // The row written at once by an upload over the limit may count no unchecked upload: that sentence is left out.
    expect(renderAlert("matcher_down", { since: facts.since, count: 0, refusalsCapped: 1 }, new Date(NOW)).sentence).not.toContain("unchecked");

    expect(ended.subject).toBe("korbat: A hold ended without a report");
    expect(paragraphs(ended.text)[0]).toBe("An admin ended the hold on a matched upload without a report at 11:00 UTC. The upload is deleted after 2026-10-20 11:00 UTC.");
    for (const mail of [r, ended]) linkless(mail);
    expect(TICK_MAILED_KINDS).toEqual(expect.arrayContaining(["matcher_down", "hold_ended_unreported"]));
  });

  test("moderation_urgent's second sentence counts the held uploads only when there are any; moderation_csam_lifted's variant on a case with a match says nobody opens such an image", () => {
    const base = { count: "2", oldest: TIME, phones: "on" };
    expect(paragraphs(renderTemplate("moderation_urgent", base).text)).not.toContain("1 matched uploads are held and wait for an admin, or hold an objection that nobody has answered.");
    expect(paragraphs(renderTemplate("moderation_urgent", { ...base, heldUploads: "3" }).text)[1]).toBe("3 matched uploads are held and wait for an admin, or hold an objection that nobody has answered.");

import { PgDialect } from "drizzle-orm/pg-core";
import type { SQL } from "drizzle-orm";
import pino from "pino";
import { describe, expect, test } from "vitest";
import { ALERT_KINDS } from "@korbat/contracts";
import type { AuthForModeration, StaffMessage } from "../src/auth";
import { MemoryStore, type RateLimitStore } from "../src/middleware/rate-limit";
import { URGENT_ALERT_KEY, URGENT_ALERT_WINDOW_MS, alertFacts, alertUrgentLane, staffAlert } from "../src/moderation/alerts";
import { createBackground, type ModerationDeps } from "../src/moderation/context";

/**
 * The staff alerts' throttle, their second leg and the work a request starts without waiting for it (3c design, sections
 * 7.1 step 5 and 7.12; 3f design, sections 5 and 7.2), without a database: the limit store is the in-memory one or a
 * stand-in that fails, the auth module a stand-in that takes, or does not take, the mail, and the database a stand-in
 * that records each statement. After the throttle, staffAlert writes one row of alert_outbox, which the watcher pushes,
 * then mails as 3c did; for 3c's and 3e's kinds, whose mail says more than the row's facts, it then marks the row mailed
 * whether or not an address took the mail, so the alert tick never renders such a mail from a row.
 */

const message: StaffMessage = { template: "moderation_urgent", count: 2, oldest: new Date("2026-10-04T06:59:59.123Z"), phones: true };
const dialect = new PgDialect();

/** What the alert needs: a store, an auth module whose mailStaff answers as scripted, a log that keeps its warnings, and a database that records. */
function world(options: { accepted?: number[]; limits?: RateLimitStore; waiting?: { n: number; oldest: string | null }; insertFails?: boolean; notify?: "on" | "off" } = {}) {
  let now = 1_000_000;
  const store = options.limits ?? new MemoryStore(() => now);
  const mails: StaffMessage[] = [];
  const warnings: string[] = [];
  const accepted = [...(options.accepted ?? [])];
  const statements: { text: string; params: unknown[] }[] = [];
  /** The order of what happened: each row written, each mail, each row marked mailed. */
  const order: string[] = [];
  let ids = 40;
  const execute = async (statement: SQL) => {
    const q = dialect.sqlToQuery(statement);
    statements.push({ text: q.sql, params: q.params });
    if (/insert into public[.]alert_outbox/.test(q.sql)) {
      if (options.insertFails) throw new Error("the database refused the row");
      order.push(`row ${q.params[0]}`);
      return [{ id: String(++ids) }];
    }
    if (/update public[.]alert_outbox set mailed_at/.test(q.sql)) {
      order.push("marked");
      return [];
    }
    // The one read the urgent alert makes: how many cases wait in the urgent lane, and since when.
    return [options.waiting ?? { n: 2, oldest: "2026-10-04T06:59:59.123Z" }];
  };
  const deps = {
    // 3f's review (people4): whether the phone alerts are on, which the urgent lane's mail says.
    config: { NOTIFY: options.notify ?? "on" } as ModerationDeps["config"],
    limits: store,
    auth: {
      mailStaff: async (sent: StaffMessage) => {
        mails.push(sent);
        order.push(`mail ${sent.template}`);
        return accepted.length > 0 ? accepted.shift()! : 1;
      },
    } as unknown as AuthForModeration,
    log: { warn: (_fields: unknown, text: string) => warnings.push(text), error: (_fields: unknown, text: string) => warnings.push(text) } as unknown as ModerationDeps["log"],
    apiDb: { execute, transaction: async <T>(run: (tx: { execute: typeof execute }) => Promise<T>) => run({ execute }) } as unknown as ModerationDeps["apiDb"],
  };
  const rows = () => statements.filter((s) => /insert into public[.]alert_outbox/.test(s.text)).map((s) => s.params);
  return { deps, mails, warnings, store, statements, order, rows, advance: (ms: number) => (now += ms) };
}

describe("a staff alert is sent at most once in its key's window", () => {
  test("the first goes, the next within the window do not, and one after the window goes again", async () => {
    const w = world();
    expect(await staffAlert(w.deps, "k", 60_000, message)).toBe("sent");
    expect(await staffAlert(w.deps, "k", 60_000, message)).toBe("throttled");
    expect(await staffAlert(w.deps, "k", 60_000, message)).toBe("throttled");
    // Another alert has a key of its own.
    expect(await staffAlert(w.deps, "other", 60_000, message)).toBe("sent");
    w.advance(60_001);
    expect(await staffAlert(w.deps, "k", 60_000, message)).toBe("sent");
    expect(w.mails).toEqual([message, message, message]);
    // A throttled alert writes no row either.
    expect(w.rows()).toHaveLength(3);
  });

  test("when no address took the mail of one of 3c's kinds, its push still goes, and the hit is given back: the next occasion mails again", async () => {

    expect(await staffAlert(w.deps, "k", 60_000, message)).toBe("sent");
    expect(await staffAlert(w.deps, "k", 60_000, message)).toBe("sent");
    expect(await staffAlert(w.deps, "k", 60_000, message)).toBe("throttled");

    expect(await staffAlert(w.deps, "k", 60_000, message)).toBe("sent");
    expect(w.warnings).toEqual(["moderation alert: the hit of an alert nobody received could not be given back"]);
  });

  test("an alert fails open: when the store cannot be reached the row and the mail go anyway, every time, and nothing is given back", async () => {
    let released = 0;

      hit: async () => {
        throw new Error("the store cannot be reached");
      },
      release: async () => {
        released++;
      },
    };
    const w = world({ accepted: [1, 0], limits });
    expect(await staffAlert(w.deps, "k", 60_000, message)).toBe("sent");
    expect(await staffAlert(w.deps, "k", 60_000, message)).toBe("sent");
    expect(w.mails).toHaveLength(2);
    expect(w.rows()).toHaveLength(2);
    expect(released).toBe(0);
    expect(w.warnings).toHaveLength(2);
  });

  test("without a key (a reveal, a decision that lifted the protection of reported images) nothing throttles it", async () => {
    const w = world();
    const reveal: StaffMessage = { template: "moderation_reveal", handle: "mod_anna", at: new Date("2026-10-04T07:00:00.000Z"), count: 1, limit: 10 };
    expect(await staffAlert(w.deps, null, 0, reveal)).toBe("sent");
    expect(await staffAlert(w.deps, null, 0, reveal)).toBe("sent");
    expect(w.mails).toEqual([reveal, reveal]);
    expect(w.rows()).toHaveLength(2);
  });
});

describe("the alert's second leg (3f design, section 7.2)", () => {
  test("the row is written first, with the kind's priority and scope and its counts and times, then the mail, then the row is marked mailed", async () => {

describe("the work a request starts and does not wait for", () => {
  test("settle resolves once every task has ended, those started meanwhile included; a task that throws is logged and stops nothing", async () => {
    const errors: unknown[] = [];
    const background = createBackground({ error: (fields: { err: unknown }) => errors.push(fields.err) } as unknown as pino.Logger);
    const done: string[] = [];
    let release!: () => void;
    const held = new Promise<void>((resolve) => {
      release = resolve;
    });
    background.start(async () => {
      await held;
      done.push("first");
      // A task may start another: settle waits for that one too.
      background.start(async () => {
        await new Promise((resolve) => setTimeout(resolve, 20));
        done.push("started meanwhile");
      });
    });
    const failure = new Error("the relay fell over");
    background.start(async () => {
      throw failure;
    });
    let settled = false;
    const settling = background.settle().then(() => {
      settled = true;
    });
    await new Promise((resolve) => setTimeout(resolve, 20));
    expect(settled).toBe(false);
    expect(errors).toEqual([failure]);
    release();
    await settling;
    expect(done).toEqual(["first", "started meanwhile"]);
    // With nothing running, settle resolves at once.
    await background.settle();
  });
});

import { describe, expect, test } from "vitest";
import { ModerationErrorCode } from "@korbat/contracts";
import { ModerationError, isModerationErrorCode, moderationErrorMessage } from "../src/moderation/context";

describe("the moderation module's refusals", () => {
  test("each of the fifty-eight codes this module raises answers with the status the design gives it (3c design, section 10; 3e design, section 10; 3f design, section 10.6; 3d design, section 10.7)", () => {
    const statuses = {
      notice_link_invalid: 422,
      notice_link_offsite: 422,
      human_check_failed: 403,
      staff_cannot_report: 403,
      notice_not_found: 404,
      already_reported: 409,
      appeal_not_open: 422,
      appeal_exists: 409,
      reexamination_not_open: 422,
      reexamination_exists: 409,
      case_changed: 409,
      case_closed: 409,
      staff_recused: 403,
      staff_target: 403,
      admin_required: 403,
      reviewer_conflict: 403,
      decision_cap: 429,
      profile_changed: 409,
      snapshot_mismatch: 409,
      snapshot_erased: 409,
      text_not_found: 409,
      invalid_decision: 422,
      text_invalid: 422,
      text_quotes_user: 422,
      image_refused: 404,
      reveal_refused: 422,
      // 3e (design, section 10.5).
      reporting_restricted: 403,
      reply_not_open: 422,
      strike_mismatch: 409,
      standing_conflict: 409,
      ground_not_established: 422,
      // 3f: a message at the contact point that already has its disposition; Task 2's order records (section 10.6).
      message_handled: 409,
      order_needs_message: 422,
      order_exists: 409,
      order_closed: 409,
      order_event_refused: 422,
      already_released: 409,
      // Task 3: giving effect, and korbat's appeal of an order's decision.
      order_changed: 409,
      order_not_verified: 422,
      order_cap: 429,
      not_appealable: 422,
      // Task 6: recovery.
      gap_mismatch: 409,
      copy_mismatch: 409,
      // 3d Task 2 (section 10.7): the release, in the order seal_release checks, and its check at commit.
      release_not_open: 409,
      release_not_reported: 422,
      release_not_quarantined: 422,
      release_preserved: 422,
      release_no_leave: 422,
      release_period_unset: 422,
      release_period_running: 422,
      release_mismatch: 409,
      // 3d Task 6 (section 10.7): "Ask for a person" that is not open, and the two refusals the automated step records on
      // its signal, which no route answers.
      objection_not_open: 422,
      // 3d review L10 (people8): a second request for a person while the first is open, as appeal_exists is.
      objection_exists: 409,
      already_protected: 409,
      automation_capped: 429,
      // 3d Task 7 (section 10.7): an end of a hold its state does not allow, one without its reason or with one too many,
      // and an image a match names, which staff are never served (answered as an image that is not shown).
      hold_not_open: 409,
      invalid_hold_end: 422,
      image_matched: 404,
    } as const;
    // The table above is the whole of the contracts' list, so a code added there fails here until its status is pinned.
    expect(Object.keys(statuses).sort()).toEqual([...ModerationErrorCode.options].sort());
    for (const [code, status] of Object.entries(statuses) as [keyof typeof statuses, number][]) {
      const err = new ModerationError(code);
      expect([err.name, err.code, err.status], code).toEqual(["ModerationError", code, status]);
      expect(err.message, code).toBe(moderationErrorMessage(code));
      expect(err.message.length, code).toBeGreaterThan(10);
      expect(isModerationErrorCode(code), code).toBe(true);
    }
    // What the audit function raises is an answer of the decision, never one of these codes.
    expect(isModerationErrorCode("staff_confirmation_ended")).toBe(false);
    expect(isModerationErrorCode("staff_confirmation_late")).toBe(false);
    // The module's own answers beside them.
    expect([new ModerationError("not_found").status, new ModerationError("invalid_request").status]).toEqual([404, 400]);
    // A session that has not finished onboarding is refused as requireSession refuses it, in the same words.
    // 3f: order_exists carries the order that stands, the one refusal with a member.
    expect(new ModerationError("order_exists", undefined, undefined, undefined, { orderId: "x" }).details).toEqual({ orderId: "x" });
    expect(new ModerationError("onboarding_required")).toMatchObject({ status: 403, message: "Choose a handle to finish setting up your account." });
    expect([new ModerationError("rate_limited").status, new ModerationError("service_unavailable").status]).toEqual([429, 503]);
  });

  test("the console's refusals say nothing about who reported: a recusal reads the same whoever the conflict concerns, and an image that is not shown gives no reason", () => {
    expect(moderationErrorMessage("staff_recused")).not.toMatch(/report/i);
    expect(moderationErrorMessage("image_refused")).toBe("That image is not shown.");
    expect(moderationErrorMessage("reveal_refused")).not.toMatch(/@|https?:/);
  });

    expect(moderationErrorMessage("appeal_exists")).toBe("You have already appealed this decision.");
    expect(moderationErrorMessage("reexamination_not_open")).toBe("A re-examination cannot be asked for this item now.");
    expect(moderationErrorMessage("reexamination_exists")).toBe("A re-examination of this item has already been asked for.");
    // The reviewer's own refusal names their part in the case, never anyone else's.
    expect(moderationErrorMessage("reviewer_conflict")).toBe("You cannot review this appeal: you took part in its case.");
    expect(moderationErrorMessage("reviewer_conflict")).not.toMatch(/report/i);
  });

  test("the words of the notice routes are written for the person reporting, and the human check names no address", () => {

    expect(moderationErrorMessage("already_reported")).toBe("You already reported this; it is being looked at.");
    for (const code of ["notice_link_invalid", "notice_link_offsite", "human_check_failed", "staff_cannot_report", "notice_not_found"] as const) {
      expect(moderationErrorMessage(code), code).not.toMatch(/@|https?:/);
    }
  });
});

import { REDRESS_TEXTS, STATEMENT_WORDS } from "@korbat/rules";
import { DecisionsList } from "../src/components/moderation/CasesLists";
import { DecisionDetail } from "../src/components/moderation/DecisionDetail";
import { messageFor } from "../src/lib/api";
import { utcMinute } from "../src/lib/moderation";
import { AUTO_WORDS } from "../src/lib/moderation-words";

/**
 * A measure a program took, as its author sees it (3d design, sections 7.10, 9.4, 9.6 and 9.7; Task 6): the decision's
 * screen with [auto.chip] beside the day and the statement of a decision without a decider; "Ask for a person" in its
 * three states, [auto.ask] with [auto.askLead], [auto.asked] with the published target and [auto.decided] with a link;
 * the row of "About you"; objection_not_open in the app's words; and the request the screen sends, read from the source.
 */
const SRC = path.resolve(import.meta.dirname, "..", "src");
const read = (...parts: string[]): string => readFileSync(path.join(SRC, ...parts), "utf8");

vi.mock("expo-router", () => ({
  Link: ({ href, children }: { href: string; children: ReactElement }) => cloneElement(children, { href } as object),
  Redirect: () => null,
  router: { push: () => undefined, replace: () => undefined },
  useLocalSearchParams: () => ({}),
  usePathname: () => "/settings/cases",
}));
vi.mock("@/lib/session", () => ({ useSession: () => ({ state: { status: "signed-out" }, refresh: async () => ({ status: "signed-out" }) }) }));
vi.mock("expo-image", async () => {
  const { createElement } = await import("react");
  return { Image: ({ source, accessibilityLabel }: { source: { uri: string }; accessibilityLabel: string }) => createElement("img", { "data-uri": source.uri, alt: accessibilityLabel }) };
});
vi.mock("react-native-reanimated", () => ({ useReducedMotion: () => false }));

const html = (element: ReactElement): string => renderToStaticMarkup(element);
/** Every run of white space: a tab, a line feed, a carriage return or a space, built from their codes. */
const SPACES = new RegExp(`[${String.fromCharCode(9, 10, 13, 32)}]+`, "g");
const textOf = (markup: string): string =>
  markup
    .replace(/<[^>]+>/g, " ")
    .replace(/&#x27;/g, "'")
    .replace(/&quot;/g, '"')
    .replace(/&amp;/g, "&")
    .replace(SPACES, " ")
    .trim();
const buttons = (markup: string): string[] => [...markup.matchAll(/<(?:div|button) [^>]*role="button"[^>]*>(.*?)<[/](?:div|button)>/g)].map((match) => textOf(match[1]!));
const id = (n: number) => `00000000-0000-4000-8000-${String(n).padStart(12, "0")}`;
const DECIDED = "2026-10-19T09:15:00.000Z";
const ASKED = "2026-10-19T10:00:00.000Z";
const noop = async () => undefined;

/** A program's withhold of an image, as the author's screen reads it, with "Ask for a person" in the state given. */
const program = (askPerson: DecisionView["askPerson"]): DecisionView => ({
  id: id(3),
  kind: "interim",
  outcome: "restricted",
  ground: "incompatible",
  ruleId: "R1",
  rulesVersion: 3,
  redressVersion: 4,
  legalReference: null,
  facts: null,
  reason: null,
  source: "own_initiative",
  decidedAt: DECIDED,
  post: { id: id(1), createdAt: "2026-10-19T08:30:00.000Z" },
  measures: [{ kind: "withhold_media", mediaId: id(2), noEffect: null, sealed: null }],
  reversals: [],
  endedMeasures: [],
  reviewed: null,
  automatedDetection: true,
  automatedDecision: "fully",
  signal: { kind: "r1_score", source: null, matchKind: null, listedAs: null, viewed: null },
  appealUntil: null,
  reversedOn: null,
  content: { kind: "post", body: "a photo", deletedByAuthor: false, images: [], imageCount: 1, imagesHidden: null },
  appeal: null,
  strike: null,
  standing: null,
  askPerson,
});

describe("a program's decision on its screen (9.4)", () => {
  test("[auto.chip] beside the day, the statement of a decision without a decider, and no appeal", () => {
    const shown = textOf(html(<DecisionDetail view={program({ state: "open" })} onAppeal={noop} onAsk={noop} />));
    expect(shown).toContain(`${AUTO_WORDS.chip}, 2026-10-19`);
    for (const sentence of [STATEMENT_WORDS.automated.until.r1, STATEMENT_WORDS.automated.fully.r1, REDRESS_TEXTS[4].askPerson!]) expect(shown).toContain(sentence);
    expect(shown).not.toContain("You can appeal this decision until");
    // A decision with a decider carries no chip.
    expect(textOf(html(<DecisionDetail view={{ ...program(null), automatedDecision: "not_automated" }} />))).not.toContain(AUTO_WORDS.chip);
  });

  test("[auto.ask] while the measure is in force and nothing was asked; its field under [auto.askLead]", () => {
    const out = html(<DecisionDetail view={program({ state: "open" })} onAsk={noop} />);
    expect(buttons(out)).toContain(AUTO_WORDS.ask);
    expect(AUTO_WORDS.askLead).toBe(
      "Write anything a person should know. You can send one message. A moderator reads it and lifts the measure or decides the case; for sealed images an admin does. You get that decision's statement either way. You do not need to cite rules or law.",
    );
    // The field's bound is the contracts' own.
    expect(OBJECTION_TEXT_MAX).toBe(2000);
    expect(read("components", "moderation", "DecisionDetail.tsx")).toContain("maxLength={OBJECTION_TEXT_MAX}");
    // Without a way to send it the screen offers no button.
    expect(buttons(html(<DecisionDetail view={program({ state: "open" })} />))).not.toContain(AUTO_WORDS.ask);
  });

  test("[auto.asked] with the time, the published target and the text as sent, and no button", () => {
    const text = "<script>alert(1)</script> It is a painting.";
    const out = html(<DecisionDetail view={program({ state: "asked", text, createdAt: ASKED })} onAsk={noop} />);
    const shown = textOf(out);
    expect(shown).toContain(AUTO_WORDS.asked(utcMinute(ASKED)));
    expect(AUTO_WORDS.asked("x")).toContain(`korbat's target is an answer within ${AUTOMATION_RULES.objectionTargetHours} hours.`);
    expect(out).not.toContain("<script>");
    expect(shown).toContain("It is a painting.");
    expect(buttons(out)).not.toContain(AUTO_WORDS.ask);
  });

  test("[auto.decided] with a link to the person's decision, and no button", () => {
    const out = html(<DecisionDetail view={program({ state: "decided", decisionId: id(9), decidedAt: ASKED })} onAsk={noop} />);
    expect(textOf(out)).toContain(AUTO_WORDS.decided(utcMinute(ASKED)));
    expect(out).toContain(`href="/settings/cases/${id(9)}"`);
    expect(buttons(out)).not.toContain(AUTO_WORDS.ask);
  });

  test("objection_not_open is [auto.decided] without the day, in the app's own words; the screen posts the text to the decision's route", () => {
    expect(ModerationErrorCode.options).toContain("objection_not_open");
    expect(messageFor("objection_not_open")).toBe(AUTO_WORDS.notOpen);
    expect(AUTO_WORDS.notOpen).toBe("A person has decided since: the decision is listed under Settings, Cases.");
    // 3d review L10 (people8): a second request while the first is open has its own code and words: nobody has decided.
    expect(ModerationErrorCode.options).toContain("objection_exists");
    expect(messageFor("objection_exists")).toBe(AUTO_WORDS.exists);
    expect(AUTO_WORDS.exists).toBe("You have already asked for a person about this decision. A person reads what you wrote.");
    expect(read("lib", "moderation.ts")).toContain("/api/moderation/decisions/${encodeURIComponent(id)}/objection`, { json: { text }, schema: DecisionView }");
    expect(read("app", "settings", "cases", "[id].tsx")).toContain("onAsk={ask}");
  });
});

describe("About you (9.6)", () => {
  test("a program's decision is listed as Taken by a program: what it did", () => {
    const row = {
      id: id(3),
      kind: "interim",
      outcome: "restricted",
      decidedOn: "2026-10-19",
      post: { id: id(1), createdAt: "2026-10-19T08:30:00.000Z" },
      actions: ["withhold_media"],
      ruleId: "R1",
      legal: false,
      appealUntil: null,
      appeal: null,
      reversedOn: null,
      endedInterim: false,
      byProgram: true,
    } as unknown as AuthorCaseRow;
    const shown = textOf(html(<DecisionsList decisions={[row]} />));
    expect(shown).toContain(AUTO_WORDS.row(""));
    expect(textOf(html(<DecisionsList decisions={[{ ...row, byProgram: false }]} />))).not.toContain(AUTO_WORDS.chip);
  });
});

import { readFileSync } from "node:fs";

import { RULES, RULES_CHANGES, RULES_VERSION } from "@korbat/rules";

vi.mock("expo-router", () => ({
  Link: ({ href, children }: { href: string; children: ReactElement }) => cloneElement(children, { href } as object),
  Redirect: () => null,
  router: { push: () => undefined, replace: () => undefined },
  useLocalSearchParams: () => ({}),
  usePathname: () => "/rules",
}));

import { RulesView } from "../src/app/rules";
import { TransparencyView } from "../src/app/transparency";
import { PAGE_DOWN, RULES_PAGE, TOOL_TEXTS, TRANSPARENCY_PAGE, toolBlocks, type AutomationLimits } from "../src/lib/public-pages";
import { MEASURES_PARAGRAPH, TERMS_SECTIONS, termsParagraphs } from "../src/lib/terms";

/**
 * The two public pages (3d design, sections 9.1 to 9.3, 10.8 and 12.2; W.1 and W.2; Task 4): server-rendered checks of
 * both pages with every tool off, with the route down and with stored editions; TOOL_TEXTS in every state a tool can be
 * in; the rules page and the terms printing their numbered sentences with the same builders; every number of the words
 * held to its constant; and the smoke test's two lead sentences held to the pages' own.
 */

const html = (element: ReactElement): string => renderToStaticMarkup(element);
/** The markup's text as a reader sees it: tags dropped, the entities React writes decoded, spaces collapsed. */
const textOf = (markup: string): string =>
  markup
    .replace(/<[^>]+>/g, " ")
    .replaceAll("&#x27;", "'")
    .replaceAll("&quot;", '"')
    .replaceAll("&gt;", ">")
    .replaceAll("&lt;", "<")
    .replaceAll("&amp;", "&")
    .replace(/ +/g, " ");

const OFF: PublicFacts = {
  r1: { state: "off", test: false, model: null, digest: null, threshold: null, thresholdVersion: null, publisherClaim: null, dpia: null, dpiaActs: null },
  match: { state: "off", test: false, source: null, dpia: null, dpiaActs: null },
  edge: { on: false, test: false },
  witness: { on: false, test: false },
  recipientsSignedOut: true,
  // 3d review M13: a keeper's address is set, as on a server ready to go public; the test of the keeper says otherwise.
  keeper: true,
};
const LIMITS: AutomationLimits = { decisionsPerHour: 20, decisionsPerDay: 100, r2DecisionsPerHour: 21, r2DecisionsPerDay: 101, unansweredMax: 22, unansweredHours: 72, refusalsPerHour: 23, objectionTargetHours: 24 };

describe("the rules page (3d Task 4)", () => {
  test("every rule with its text and its lists, the law, the measures and the numbered sections, every tool off, and the change log newest first", () => {
    const markup = html(<RulesView facts={OFF} />);
    const text = textOf(markup);
    expect(text).toContain(RULES_PAGE.lead);
    for (const rule of RULES) {
      expect(text).toContain(`${rule.id}: ${rule.title}`);
      expect(text).toContain(rule.text);
      for (const item of [...rule.allowed, ...rule.notAllowed]) expect(text).toContain(item);
    }
    expect(text).toContain(RULES_PAGE.law);
    expect(text).toContain(MEASURES_PARAGRAPH);
    for (const tool of [TOOL_TEXTS.r1.off, TOOL_TEXTS.match.off, TOOL_TEXTS.edge.off, TOOL_TEXTS.witness.off, RULES_PAGE.autoNone]) expect(text).toContain(tool);
    expect(text).not.toContain(PAGE_DOWN);
    expect(text).toContain(RULES_PAGE.version(RULES_VERSION));
    const changes = [...RULES_CHANGES].reverse().map((change) => text.indexOf(RULES_PAGE.change(change)));
    expect(changes.every((at) => at > -1)).toBe(true);
    expect([...changes].sort((a, b) => a - b)).toEqual(changes);
    // The headings, each a header of its level, and the links to the other page and to How Explore works.
    for (const heading of [RULES_PAGE.rulesHeading, RULES_PAGE.measuresHeading, RULES_PAGE.automationHeading, RULES_PAGE.versionHeading]) expect(markup).toContain(`aria-level="2"`);
    expect(markup).toContain('href="/transparency"');
    expect(markup).toContain('href="/explore/about"');
  });

  test("the numbered sentences are the terms' own: the same builders print Strikes, Suspension, Reporting in bad faith and Terrorist content in both", () => {
    const text = textOf(html(<RulesView facts={OFF} />));
    for (const title of ["Strikes", "Suspension and termination", "Reporting in bad faith", "Terrorist content"]) {
      const section = TERMS_SECTIONS.find((candidate) => candidate.title === title);
      expect(section, title).toBeDefined();
      for (const paragraph of termsParagraphs(section!.body)) expect(text).toContain(paragraph);
    }
    const decide = TERMS_SECTIONS.find((section) => section.title === "How moderators decide")!;
    expect(termsParagraphs(decide.body)).toContain(MEASURES_PARAGRAPH);
  });

  test("while the facts are read the automation section holds its lead alone; when the route does not answer it reads [page.down] and prints no tool as off or on", () => {
    for (const [facts, down] of [["loading", false], ["down", true]] as const) {
      const text = textOf(html(<RulesView facts={facts} />));
      expect(text).toContain(RULES_PAGE.autoLead);
      expect(text.includes(PAGE_DOWN)).toBe(down);
      for (const tool of [TOOL_TEXTS.r1.off, TOOL_TEXTS.match.off, TOOL_TEXTS.edge.off, TOOL_TEXTS.witness.off, RULES_PAGE.autoNone]) expect(text).not.toContain(tool);
      expect(text).toContain(RULES_PAGE.lead);
    }
  });

  test("with a tool that rates or compares images on, the caps and the target from the limits, and no [rules.auto.none]", () => {
    const on = { ...OFF, match: { state: "alerts", test: true, source: "test", dpia: "2026-10-01", dpiaActs: null } } as PublicFacts;
    const text = textOf(html(<RulesView facts={on} limits={LIMITS} />));
    expect(text).toContain(RULES_PAGE.autoCap(LIMITS));
    expect(text).toContain(RULES_PAGE.autoTarget(LIMITS.objectionTargetHours));
    expect(text).not.toContain(RULES_PAGE.autoNone);
    expect(RULES_PAGE.autoCap(LIMITS)).toContain("at most 20 measures an hour and 100 a day under rule R1, and at most 21 an hour and 101 a day under rule R2");
    expect(RULES_PAGE.autoCap(LIMITS)).toContain("while 22 of its measures");
    expect(RULES_PAGE.autoCap(LIMITS)).toContain("refuses at most 23 uploads an hour");
  });

  test("3d Task 6: the page passes the contracts' AUTOMATION_RULES as its limits, so the caps it prints are the database's", () => {
    const source = readFileSync(path.resolve(import.meta.dirname, "../src/app/rules.tsx"), "utf8");
    expect(source).toContain("<RulesView facts={facts} limits={AUTOMATION_RULES} />");
    const on = { ...OFF, r1: { ...OFF.r1, state: "withholds", test: true } } as PublicFacts;
    const text = textOf(html(<RulesView facts={on} limits={AUTOMATION_RULES} />));
    expect(text).toContain(RULES_PAGE.autoCap(AUTOMATION_RULES));
    expect(text).toContain(RULES_PAGE.autoTarget(AUTOMATION_RULES.objectionTargetHours));
    expect(RULES_PAGE.autoCap(AUTOMATION_RULES)).toContain(`at most ${AUTOMATION_RULES.decisionsPerHour} measures an hour and ${AUTOMATION_RULES.decisionsPerDay} a day under rule R1`);
  });
});

describe("TOOL_TEXTS in each state (3d Task 4, W.1)", () => {
  const blockOf = (facts: PublicFacts, tool: string) => toolBlocks(facts).find((block) => block.tool === tool)!;

  test("every tool off, as the facts route answers until the tasks that build them: each block its off text alone", () => {
    expect(toolBlocks(OFF).map((block) => [block.tool, block.on, block.paragraphs])).toEqual([

      ["edge", false, [TOOL_TEXTS.edge.off]],

    expect(seals.paragraphs).toEqual([TOOL_TEXTS.match.seals("test").replace(": on,", ": on (test adapter),"), RULES_PAGE.dpia("2026-10-03"), RULES_PAGE.dpiaActs("2026-10-04")]);

    // While on, the rating and the fingerprints are kept with the image; once off, none from the time it was on.
    expect(TOOL_TEXTS.r1.flags).toContain("korbat keeps the rating with the image");
    expect(TOOL_TEXTS.r1.withholds).toContain("korbat keeps the rating with the image");
    expect(TOOL_TEXTS.r1.off).toContain("korbat keeps no rating from a time when one did");

  });

  test("no text says more than is known: never that an image is such material, that korbat confirmed it, or the same fingerprint of a picture's look", () => {
    const texts = [

describe("the transparency page (3d Task 4)", () => {
  const empty: TransparencyFigures = {
    restrictions: { byGround: [], byMeasure: [], total: "0" },

    for (const line of ["The law: about 10", "Other grounds: about 10", "All restrictions: about 80", "Remove: about 70", "Other measures: 1 to 9", "Decisions that found no breach: about 140"]) expect(text).toContain(line);
    for (const line of ["Reports under korbat's rules: about 30", "Notices of illegal content (Article 16 of the Digital Services Act): about 10", "Decision kept: about 10", "No action again: about 20", "Strike: about 10"]) expect(text).toContain(line);

    // The standing sentence under every year, whether or not it has the section.

    expect(text).toContain(TRANSPARENCY_PAGE.recipients("2026-02", "about 120", "about 340"));
    expect(text).toContain(TRANSPARENCY_PAGE.recipientsOff("2025-02", "1 to 9"));

    expect(markup).toContain('href="/rules"');

  test("a correction says so with its day; no edition yet reads [tr.none]; a route that does not answer reads [page.down] beside the fixed texts", () => {

    );
    expect(TRANSPARENCY_PAGE.recipientsNotRecorded("2025-02")).toContain(`: ${TRANSPARENCY_PAGE.notRecorded}.`);
    expect(text).not.toContain("has not counted six full months yet");
    expect(Object.keys(TRANSPARENCY_PAGE)).not.toContain("recipientsNotYet");
  });

  test("review L13 (people11): the table of uploads not accepted prints its total first, Uploads refused on a match, then the fates", () => {
    const uploads: TransparencyFigures["uploads"] = [
      { label: "refused", count: "about 20" },
      { label: "report", count: "about 10" },
      { label: "other", count: "1 to 9" },
    ];
    const text = textOf(html(<TransparencyView answer={{ editions: [{ ...answer.editions[1]!, figures: { ...empty, uploads } }] }} />));
    const total = text.indexOf("Uploads refused on a match: about 20");
    expect(total).toBeGreaterThan(text.indexOf(TRANSPARENCY_PAGE.tables.uploads));
    expect(text.indexOf("Held for a report: about 10")).toBeGreaterThan(total);
    expect(text.indexOf("Other: 1 to 9", total)).toBeGreaterThan(total);
  });

  test("every number of the page's words is its constant's: the due day, the floor, the rounding, the salt's hours; the recipients' last month is the one before the due day", () => {
    expect(TRANSPARENCY_PAGE.read).toContain(`on or after ${TRANSPARENCY_RULES.dueDay} March of the next year`);
    expect(TRANSPARENCY_PAGE.read).toContain(`korbat prints 0, "1 to ${TRANSPARENCY_RULES.floor - 1}"`);
    expect(TRANSPARENCY_PAGE.read).toContain("rounded to the nearest ten");
    expect(TRANSPARENCY_PAGE.read).toContain("fewer than ten");
    expect(TRANSPARENCY_PAGE.none).toContain(`${TRANSPARENCY_RULES.dueDay} March`);
    expect(TRANSPARENCY_PAGE.method(1)).toContain(`exists for ${RECIPIENT_RULES.saltHours} hours`);
    expect(TRANSPARENCY_PAGE.read).not.toContain("1 June");

describe("the transparency page's daily value (3d Task 5, 9.3 item 6, W.2)", () => {
  const value = (c: string) => c.repeat(64);
  const head: PublicHead = {
    days: [
      { day: "2026-10-19", kind: "head", value: value("a"), witness: "rfc3161", token: "MAMCAQA=", retiredOn: null, lastDay: null },
      { day: "2026-10-18", kind: "restore", value: value("b"), witness: "none", token: null, retiredOn: null, lastDay: "2026-10-15" },
      { day: "2026-10-17", kind: "head", value: value("c"), witness: "none", token: null, retiredOn: "2026-10-18", lastDay: null },
      { day: "2026-10-15", kind: "head", value: value("d"), witness: "none", token: null, retiredOn: null, lastDay: null },
    ],
  };
  const T = TRANSPARENCY_PAGE;

  test("its section stands after the editions and before the Transparency Database: [tr.head], a row a day newest first with its value and its witness, [tr.restore], [tr.retired] and [tr.headMissing] in their places", () => {
    const text = textOf(html(<TransparencyView answer={{ editions: [] }} head={head} />));
    const at = (part: string) => {
      expect(text, part).toContain(part);
      return text.indexOf(part);
    };
    const order = [
      at(T.none),
      at(T.headHeading),
      at(T.head),
      at(T.headRow("2026-10-19", value("a"), "rfc3161")),
      at(T.restore("2026-10-18", "2026-10-15")),
      at(T.headMissingRow("2026-10-18")),
      at(`${T.headRow("2026-10-17", value("c"), "none")} ${T.retired("2026-10-18")}`),
      at(T.headMissingRow("2026-10-16")),
      at(T.headRow("2026-10-15", value("d"), "none")),
      at(T.tdbHeading),
    ];
    expect([...order].sort((a, b) => a - b)).toEqual(order);
    // A restore that found nothing that still fits says so; a day after the newest row is not shown as missing.
    expect(T.restore("2026-10-18", null)).toBe("2026-10-18: korbat restored its database from a backup. No value above still fits the restored log.");
    expect(text).not.toContain(T.headMissingRow("2026-10-20"));
    expect(text).not.toContain(T.headMissingRow("2026-10-14"));
    // A public page points at no person, and the head's place is in no row.
    expect(text).not.toMatch(/@|chainSeq|chain_seq|Place:/);
  });

  test("while a shown row has a proof: [tr.verify] as the lab ran it, with that day's value and file, and the proof to download as <day>.tsr; without one, neither", () => {
    const markup = html(<TransparencyView answer={{ editions: [] }} head={head} />);
    const text = textOf(markup);
    expect(text).toContain(T.verify(value("a"), "2026-10-19"));
    expect(T.verify(value("a"), "2026-10-19")).toBe(
      `To check a day: download its proof, get the timestamp authority's certificates from the authority itself, and run: openssl ts -verify -digest ${value("a")} -in 2026-10-19.tsr -CAfile <certificates>. It answers "Verification: OK" when that authority signed this value at the time the proof states.`,
    );
    expect(text).toContain(T.download("2026-10-19"));
    // One row has a proof, so one download: the words before the day are the same for every row.
    expect(text.split(T.download("DAY").split("DAY")[0]!).length - 1).toBe(1);
    const unwitnessed: PublicHead = { days: head.days.map((row) => ({ ...row, witness: "none", token: null })) };
    const plain = textOf(html(<TransparencyView answer={{ editions: [] }} head={unwitnessed} />));
    expect(plain).not.toContain("openssl");
    expect(plain).not.toContain(T.download("2026-10-19"));
    expect(plain).toContain(T.headRow("2026-10-19", value("a"), "none"));
  });

  test("review L15 (people13): a test adapter's token turns on neither [tr.verify] nor a download; only a row witnessed by rfc3161 does", () => {
    const tested: PublicHead = { days: head.days.map((row) => (row.day === "2026-10-19" ? { ...row, witness: "test" as const } : row)) };
    const text = textOf(html(<TransparencyView answer={{ editions: [] }} head={tested} />));
    expect(text).toContain(T.headRow("2026-10-19", value("a"), "test"));
    expect(text).not.toContain("openssl");
    expect(text).not.toContain(T.download("2026-10-19"));
    // A newer test row and an older rfc3161 row: the check and the one download are the older row's.
    const mixed: PublicHead = {
      days: [
        { day: "2026-10-20", kind: "head", value: value("e"), witness: "test", token: "MAMCAQA=", retiredOn: null, lastDay: null },
        ...head.days,
      ],
    };
    const both = textOf(html(<TransparencyView answer={{ editions: [] }} head={mixed} />));
    expect(both).toContain(T.verify(value("a"), "2026-10-19"));
    expect(both).not.toContain(T.verify(value("e"), "2026-10-20"));
    expect(both).toContain(T.download("2026-10-19"));
    expect(both).not.toContain(T.download("2026-10-20"));
  });

  test("[page.down] for this part alone; no value yet reads its sentence; while it loads, the section holds [tr.head] alone", () => {
    const down = textOf(html(<TransparencyView answer={{ editions: [] }} head="down" />));
    expect(down).toContain(T.none);
    expect(down.split(PAGE_DOWN).length - 1).toBe(1);
    expect(down.indexOf(PAGE_DOWN)).toBeGreaterThan(down.indexOf(T.head));
    const both = textOf(html(<TransparencyView answer="down" head="down" />));
    expect(both.split(PAGE_DOWN).length - 1).toBe(2);
    expect(textOf(html(<TransparencyView answer={{ editions: [] }} head={{ days: [] }} />))).toContain(T.headNone);
    const loading = textOf(html(<TransparencyView answer={{ editions: [] }} head="loading" />));
    expect(loading).toContain(T.head);
    expect(loading).not.toContain(PAGE_DOWN);
    expect(loading).not.toContain(T.headNone);
  });

  test("review M13: the keeper's sentence follows [tr.head] only while a keeper's address is set; without one the page names no person; until the facts answer, neither", () => {
    const withKeeper = textOf(html(<TransparencyView answer={{ editions: [] }} head={head} keeper={true} />));
    expect(withKeeper).toContain(`${T.head} ${T.headKeeper}`);
    const without = textOf(html(<TransparencyView answer={{ editions: [] }} head={head} keeper={false} />));
    expect(without).toContain(`${T.head} ${T.headNoKeeper}`);
    expect(without).not.toContain("a person who does not run the server");
    const unknown = textOf(html(<TransparencyView answer={{ editions: [] }} head={head} />));
    expect(unknown).not.toContain(T.headKeeper);
    expect(unknown).not.toContain(T.headNoKeeper);
    // The page asks the facts route too, for the keeper's member alone.
    const source = readFileSync(path.resolve(import.meta.dirname, "../src/app/transparency.tsx"), "utf8");
    expect(source).toContain('api("/api/public/facts", { schema: PublicFacts })');
  });

  test("its words are W.2's: [tr.head], [tr.headMissing], [tr.restore] and [tr.retired]", () => {
    expect(T.head).toBe(
      "Each day korbat publishes one value computed from the day and the newest entry of its staff audit log, the record of everything korbat's staff confirm with their keys. If an earlier entry were changed or removed later, the log would no longer lead to the values published since. A value shows neither how many entries the log has nor any entry, and it differs from one day to the next also when nothing was added to the log. A value on korbat's own page proves nothing against korbat's operator, who could change this page too.",
    );
    // 3d review M13: the sentence that names the keeper, and the one printed in its place while no address is set.
    expect(T.headKeeper).toBe("So the same value goes each day to a person who does not run the server, and, when the outside timestamp is on, to a timestamp authority.");
    expect(T.headNoKeeper).toBe("When the outside timestamp is on, the same value goes each day to a timestamp authority.");
    expect(T.headMissingRow("2026-10-16")).toBe("2026-10-16: no value was published");
    expect(T.restore("2026-10-18", "2026-10-15")).toBe("2026-10-18: korbat restored its database from a backup. The newest value above that still fits the restored log is of 2026-10-15.");
    expect(T.retired("2026-10-18")).toBe("retired by the restore of 2026-10-18: true when published, and fits no log now");
  });
});

describe("the smoke test looks for the pages' own lead sentences in the bundle (3d Task 4, 12.2)", () => {

import { cloneElement, type ReactElement } from "react";
import { renderToStaticMarkup } from "react-dom/server";
import { describe, expect, test, vi } from "vitest";
import type { ReleaseNoticeView } from "@korbat/contracts";
import { RELEASE_NOTICE, releaseNoticeParagraphs } from "@korbat/rules";
import { NoticesList } from "../src/components/moderation/CasesLists";
import { ReleaseNoticeDetail } from "../src/components/moderation/ReleaseNotice";
import { RELEASE_TEXTS } from "../src/lib/moderation-words";

/**
 * A release of sealed images as its author reads it (3d design, sections 7.2, 9.6 and W.6; Task 2): the notice's screen
 * prints RELEASE_NOTICE's paragraphs and no control, links the decision that sealed, and says through the paragraph on
 * that decision where its appeal stands (3d review L11); "About you" lists the release as "Sealed images released" with its day. Nothing names an
 * authority, a reference or an assessment, and no image is drawn.
 */
vi.mock("expo-router", () => ({
  Link: ({ href, children }: { href: string; children: ReactElement }) => cloneElement(children, { href } as object),
  router: { push: () => undefined },
}));

const html = (element: ReactElement): string => renderToStaticMarkup(element);
const textOf = (markup: string): string => markup.replace(/<[^>]+>/g, " ").replace(/&#x27;/g, "'").replace(/&quot;/g, '"').replace(/ +/g, " ").trim();

const view: ReleaseNoticeView = {
  id: "1a2b3c4d-0000-4000-8000-000000000001",
  basis: "leave",
  releasedAt: "2026-10-18T10:05:00.000Z",
  backupsClearAt: "2026-11-17T10:05:00.000Z",
  upload: false,
  posts: [{ id: "1a2b3c4d-0000-4000-8000-000000000002", createdAt: "2026-09-01T08:30:00.000Z" }],
  postCount: 1,
  images: 2,
  sealDecisionId: "1a2b3c4d-0000-4000-8000-000000000003",
  appeal: "none",
};

describe("a release's notice in the app (3d Task 2)", () => {
  test("the screen prints the notice's paragraphs, links the decision that sealed, and offers no control", () => {
    const markup = html(<ReleaseNoticeDetail view={view} />);
    const shown = textOf(markup);
    for (const paragraph of releaseNoticeParagraphs(view)) expect(shown).toContain(textOf(paragraph));
    expect(shown).toContain(RELEASE_TEXTS.title);
    expect(markup).toContain(`/settings/cases/${view.sealDecisionId}`);
    expect(shown).not.toContain(RELEASE_NOTICE.seal.pending);
    expect(markup).not.toMatch(/<img|<button/);
    expect(shown).not.toMatch(/no longer holds|destroyed|assessed|illegal|reference/i);
  });

  test("3d review L11 (people9): while an appeal of the sealing decision waits, the notice's own paragraph says so, once; an answered one is not called open", () => {
    const pending = textOf(html(<ReleaseNoticeDetail view={{ ...view, appeal: "pending" }} />));
    expect(pending).toContain(textOf(RELEASE_NOTICE.seal.pending));
    expect(pending.split("still open").length).toBe(2);
    const answered = textOf(html(<ReleaseNoticeDetail view={{ ...view, appeal: "answered" }} />));
    expect(answered).toContain(textOf(RELEASE_NOTICE.seal.answered));
    expect(answered).not.toContain("still open");
    // The screen prints no line of its own about the appeal: the paragraph is the one the mail sent.
    expect(Object.keys(RELEASE_TEXTS)).not.toContain("appeal");
  });

  test('"About you" lists a release as "Sealed images released" with its day, linking its notice, and nothing while there is none', () => {
    const markup = html(<NoticesList notices={[{ kind: "release", id: view.id, at: view.releasedAt }]} />);
    expect(textOf(markup)).toContain(`${RELEASE_TEXTS.entry} ${RELEASE_TEXTS.entryOn("2026-10-18")}`);
    expect(markup).toContain(`/settings/cases/releases/${view.id}`);
    expect(html(<NoticesList notices={[]} />)).toBe("");
    expect(RELEASE_NOTICE.what).toContain("A person did this, not a program.");
  });
});

describe("laneFor", () => {
  const TC: TdbCategory = "STATEMENT_CATEGORY_OTHER_VIOLATION_TC";

  test("a rule report takes its rule's lane: R2 and R5 are urgent, R3 and R4 next, R1 and R6 last", () => {
    const lanes = RULE_IDS.map((ruleId) => laneFor({ ruleId, allegesIllegal: false, csam: false, category: TC }));

    expect(laneFor({ ruleId: null, allegesIllegal: false, csam: true, category: TC })).toBe(0);
  });

  test("a notice of illegality takes its category's lane, for every category", () => {
    const urgent = ["STATEMENT_CATEGORY_VIOLENCE", "STATEMENT_CATEGORY_RISK_FOR_PUBLIC_SECURITY", "STATEMENT_CATEGORY_SELF_HARM"];
    const next = [

      "STATEMENT_CATEGORY_CYBER_VIOLENCE",
      "STATEMENT_CATEGORY_CYBER_VIOLENCE_AGAINST_WOMEN",

      "STATEMENT_CATEGORY_NOT_SPECIFIED_NOTICE",
    ];
    for (const category of TDB_CATEGORIES) {

      expect(laneFor({ ruleId: null, allegesIllegal: true, csam: false, category }), category).toBe(expected);
    }
  });

  test("a notice of illegality that also cites a rule takes the more severe of the two lanes", () => {

describe("the order of a decision's actions", () => {

    const sorted: DecisionActionParams[] = [
      { kind: "remove", mediaId: null },
      { kind: "remove_media", mediaId: a },
      { kind: "remove_media", mediaId: b },
      { kind: "reset_bio", mediaId: null },
      { kind: "seal_media", mediaId: null },
      { kind: "withhold_media", mediaId: a },
    ];
    for (const shuffled of [[...sorted].reverse(), [sorted[3]!, sorted[0]!, sorted[5]!, sorted[2]!, sorted[1]!, sorted[4]!]]) {
      expect([...shuffled].sort(compareDecisionActions)).toEqual(sorted);
    }
    expect(compareDecisionActions(sorted[1]!, sorted[1]!)).toBe(0);
    expect(compareDecisionActions({ kind: "restore_media", mediaId: null }, { kind: "restore_media", mediaId: a })).toBeLessThan(0);
  });
});

    expect(TEXT_DIGEST_TAG).toBe("korbat.text.v1");
  });

  test.each(TEXT_DIGEST_VECTORS.map((vector) => [vector.name, vector] as const))("%s: the sha256 of the tag, a line feed, the salt's bytes and the text's UTF-8 bytes", async (_name, vector) => {
    expect(await textDigest(vector.salt, vector.text)).toBe(vector.digest);
  });

  test("the longest vector is 5000 UTF-16 units, and the vectors hold a line feed, a character outside ASCII and one outside the basic plane", () => {
    expect(Math.max(...TEXT_DIGEST_VECTORS.map((vector) => vector.text.length))).toBe(5000);
    const all = TEXT_DIGEST_VECTORS.map((vector) => vector.text).join("");
    expect(all).toContain(LF);
    expect(all).toContain(E_ACUTE);
    expect(all).toContain(GRINNING);
  });

  test("another salt or another text gives another digest", async () => {
    const digests = await Promise.all([textDigest("a1".repeat(32), "one"), textDigest("a2".repeat(32), "one"), textDigest("a1".repeat(32), "one "), textDigest("a1".repeat(32), "One")]);
    expect(new Set(digests).size).toBe(4);
  });

  test("a salt that is not 32 bytes of lower-case hex is refused, never padded or folded", async () => {
    for (const salt of ["", "a1".repeat(31), "a1".repeat(33), "A1".repeat(32), "g1".repeat(32), ` ${"a1".repeat(32)}`]) {
      await expect(textDigest(salt, "text"), JSON.stringify(salt)).rejects.toThrow(TypeError);
    }
  });

  test("a text with a lone surrogate, which has no UTF-8 bytes, is refused rather than hashed as something else", async () => {
    const high = String.fromCharCode(0xd83d);
    const low = String.fromCharCode(0xde00);
    for (const text of [high, low, `a${high}b`, `${low}${high}`]) await expect(textDigest("a1".repeat(32), text)).rejects.toThrow(TypeError);
    // The pair itself is a character.
    await expect(textDigest("a1".repeat(32), `${high}${low}`)).resolves.toMatch(/^[0-9a-f]{64}$/);
  });
});

describe("snapshotText and snapshotDigest", () => {
  const post: SnapshotDigestInput = {
    salt: "ab".repeat(32),

    replyToId: null,
    quoteOfId: null,
    body: null,
    media: null,
    displayName: `Bob ${GRINNING}`,
    bio: "",
    handle: "bob",
  };
  const BS = String.fromCharCode(92);
  // The texts and the digests below were computed with Python's json and hashlib when they were written.
  const POST_TEXT =
    `{"authorHandle":"ada","bio":null,"body":"Line one${BS}ncaf${E_ACUTE} ${GRINNING}","displayName":null,"handle":null,` +
    `"media":[{"alt":"A cat","height":800,"id":"11111111-2222-4333-8444-555555555555","width":1200},{"alt":null,"height":480,"id":"66666666-7777-4888-9999-aaaaaaaaaaaa","width":640}],` +
    `"postCreatedAt":"2026-10-01T08:30:00.000Z","postState":"visible","quoteOfId":"7e2d9a10-6c3b-4f5e-8a21-0d4c7b9e1f36","replyToId":null,` +
    `"salt":"${"ab".repeat(32)}","takenAt":"2026-10-03T10:00:00.123Z","targetId":"3f1c2b1e-8d4a-4c1e-9b2a-6f0e5d4c3b2a","targetType":"post","v":1}`;
  const POST_DIGEST = "cb995d11ed14e3c4e555c187d319a86506b263e98f924f59f2f7d5231a3bc6e6";
  const ACCOUNT_DIGEST = "41019b2a47d4ebad37cc8c5ad25f8d79a7232c4e3e705231f9e9ba1e02fb1f26";

  test("the tag names the version of the rule", () => {
    expect(SNAPSHOT_DIGEST_TAG).toBe("korbat.snapshot.v1");
  });

  test("the text is the sorted JSON of version 1 and the snapshot's fifteen members", () => {
    expect(snapshotText(post)).toBe(POST_TEXT);
    const parsed = JSON.parse(snapshotText(account)) as Record<string, unknown>;
    expect(Object.keys(parsed)).toEqual(["authorHandle", "bio", "body", "displayName", "handle", "media", "postCreatedAt", "postState", "quoteOfId", "replyToId", "salt", "takenAt", "targetId", "targetType", "v"]);
    expect(parsed).toEqual({ v: 1, ...account });
  });

  test("the digest is the sha256 of the tag, a line feed and that text", async () => {
    expect(await snapshotDigest(post)).toBe(POST_DIGEST);
    expect(await snapshotDigest(account)).toBe(ACCOUNT_DIGEST);
  });

  test("it round-trips the snapshot answer's JSON, whatever order and whatever else the answer carries", async () => {
    // As the console receives it: parsed from JSON, with members the digest does not cover, in another order.
    const sent = {
      id: "9d0f5e3c-0000-4000-8000-000000000001",
      digest: POST_DIGEST,
      withheld: false,
      erasedAt: null,
      ...Object.fromEntries(Object.entries(post).reverse()),
      media: post.media!.map((image) => ({ height: image.height, width: image.width, note: "never part of a snapshot", alt: image.alt, id: image.id })),
    };
    const answer = JSON.parse(JSON.stringify(sent)) as SnapshotDigestInput;
    expect(snapshotText(answer)).toBe(POST_TEXT);
    expect(await snapshotDigest(answer)).toBe(POST_DIGEST);
  });

  test("any member that changes gives another digest", async () => {
    const changed: SnapshotDigestInput[] = [
      { ...post, salt: "ac".repeat(32) },
      { ...post, takenAt: "2026-10-03T10:00:00.124Z" },
      { ...post, body: `${post.body} ` },
      { ...post, postState: "withheld" },
      { ...post, quoteOfId: null },
      { ...post, media: [post.media![1]!, post.media![0]!] },
      { ...post, media: [{ ...post.media![0]!, alt: "A dog" }, post.media![1]!] },
      { ...post, authorHandle: "adb" },
    ];
    const digests = await Promise.all([post, ...changed].map(snapshotDigest));
    expect(new Set(digests).size).toBe(changed.length + 1);
  });

  test("a time that is not the UTC string toISOString writes, to the millisecond, is refused", () => {
    for (const takenAt of ["2026-10-03T10:00:00Z", "2026-10-03T10:00:00.123456Z", "2026-10-03T12:00:00.123+02:00", "2026-10-03 10:00:00.123Z", ""]) {
      expect(() => snapshotText({ ...post, takenAt }), takenAt).toThrow(TypeError);
    }
    expect(() => snapshotText({ ...post, postCreatedAt: "2026-10-01T08:30:00Z" })).toThrow(TypeError);
    expect(snapshotText({ ...post, takenAt: new Date(Date.UTC(2026, 9, 3, 10, 0, 0, 123)).toISOString() })).toBe(POST_TEXT);
  });
});

describe("appealDeadline", () => {
  const at = (iso: string) => new Date(iso);
  const deadline = (iso: string) => appealDeadline(at(iso)).toISOString();

  test("six calendar months later, at the same UTC time", () => {
    expect(deadline("2026-10-03T10:15:30.250Z")).toBe("2027-04-03T10:15:30.250Z");
    expect(deadline("2026-01-15T00:00:00.000Z")).toBe("2026-07-15T00:00:00.000Z");
    expect(deadline("2026-07-01T23:59:59.999Z")).toBe("2027-01-01T23:59:59.999Z");
  });

  test("a day the sixth month lacks becomes that month's last day", () => {
    // 31 August plus six months is the end of February: the 28th, or the 29th in a leap year.
    expect(deadline("2026-08-31T12:00:00.000Z")).toBe("2027-02-28T12:00:00.000Z");
    expect(deadline("2027-08-31T12:00:00.000Z")).toBe("2028-02-29T12:00:00.000Z");
    expect(deadline("2027-08-30T12:00:00.000Z")).toBe("2028-02-29T12:00:00.000Z");
    expect(deadline("2027-08-29T12:00:00.000Z")).toBe("2028-02-29T12:00:00.000Z");
    expect(deadline("2026-03-31T08:00:00.000Z")).toBe("2026-09-30T08:00:00.000Z");
    expect(deadline("2026-05-31T08:00:00.000Z")).toBe("2026-11-30T08:00:00.000Z");
    expect(deadline("2026-10-31T08:00:00.000Z")).toBe("2027-04-30T08:00:00.000Z");
    expect(deadline("2026-12-31T08:00:00.000Z")).toBe("2027-06-30T08:00:00.000Z");
    // A leap day itself moves to 29 August: August has the day.
    expect(deadline("2028-02-29T08:00:00.000Z")).toBe("2028-08-29T08:00:00.000Z");
  });

  test("it is computed in UTC: the last instants of a UTC month stay on that month's side", () => {
    expect(deadline("2026-08-31T23:59:59.999Z")).toBe("2027-02-28T23:59:59.999Z");
    expect(deadline("2026-09-01T00:00:00.000Z")).toBe("2027-03-01T00:00:00.000Z");
  });

  test("it leaves its argument as it was", () => {
    const informed = at("2026-08-31T12:00:00.000Z");
    appealDeadline(informed);
    expect(informed.toISOString()).toBe("2026-08-31T12:00:00.000Z");
  });
});
